options.label: C
options.text: Ratification by half the States under Article 368

options.label: D
options.text: A referendum in the affected State

questions.solution: Correct answer: Recommendation of the President and reference to State Legislature (views not binding).

questions.text: Which case held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution and can be amended subject to the basic structure doctrine?

options.label: A
options.text: Re Berubari Union (1960)

options.label: B
options.text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

options.label: C
options.text: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)

options.label: D
options.text: Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973).

questions.text: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 provides for expedited naturalisation for persecuted minorities from which three countries?

options.label: A
options.text: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar

options.label: B
options.text: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan

options.label: C
options.text: Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka

options.label: D
options.text: Afghanistan, Pakistan, Myanmar

questions.solution: Correct answer: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan.

questions.text: The removal of the head of a constitutional body such as the Comptroller and Auditor General is governed by which procedure?

options.label: A
options.text: Simple majority resolution in Parliament

options.label: B
options.text: Impeachment as prescribed in the Constitution

options.label: C
options.text: Executive order by the President on advice of the Council of Ministers

options.label: D
options.text: Judicial review by the Supreme Court

questions.solution: Correct answer: Impeachment as prescribed in the Constitution.

questions.text: In its 2009 judgment Election Commission of India v. Union of India, the Supreme Court held that the appointment of Election Commissioners requires consultation with which authority?

options.label: A
options.text: Prime Minister

options.label: B
options.text: Leader of Opposition

options.label: C
options.text: Chief Justice of India

options.label: D
options.text: President

questions.solution: Correct answer: Chief Justice of India.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes a power of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)?

options.label: A
options.text: It can initiate criminal proceedings against violators

options.label: B
options.text: Its recommendations are binding on the government

options.label: C
options.text: It can approach the Supreme Court or High Courts for enforcement of its recommendations

options.label: D
options.text: It has the authority to remove public servants from office

questions.solution: Correct answer: It can approach the Supreme Court or High Courts for enforcement of its recommendations.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the legal status and enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) in India?

options.label: A
options.text: The MCC is a statutory law enacted by Parliament and violations are tried in criminal courts.

options.label: B
options.text: The MCC comes into force only after the polling process has concluded.

options.label: C
options.text: The MCC is a non‑statutory set of guidelines enforced by the Election Commission under Article 324, a position upheld by the Supreme Court.

options.label: D
options.text: The Election Commission has no authority to act on MCC violations; only the judiciary can intervene.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The MCC is a non‑statutory set of guidelines enforced by the Election Commission under Article 324, a position upheld by the Supreme Court..

questions.text: Regarding the Comptroller and Auditor General’s (CAG) performance audit reports, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Performance audit reports are legally binding on the executive and automatically trigger penal action.

options.label: B
options.text: Performance audit reports are advisory in nature and require the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) to take follow‑up action.

options.label: C
options.text: Performance audit replaces the traditional financial audit and eliminates the need for compliance audit.

options.label: D
options.text: The CAG’s performance audit findings are directly enforceable by the Supreme Court without legislative intervention.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Performance audit reports are advisory in nature and require the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) to take follow‑up action..

questions.text: What was the Supreme Court’s 2022 ruling concerning lateral entry into the civil services?

options.label: A
options.text: Lateral entry violates Article 320 and is therefore unconstitutional.

options.label: B
options.text: Consultation with the UPSC is mandatory, but the UPSC does not have exclusive control over lateral entry appointments.

options.label: C
options.text: The UPSC must conduct all lateral entry examinations and approve every appointment.

options.label: D
options.text: Lateral entry can only be introduced through a constitutional amendment.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Consultation with the UPSC is mandatory, but the UPSC does not have exclusive control over lateral entry appointments..

questions.text: Which set of criteria were introduced by the Fifteenth Finance Commission for horizontal devolution among States?

options.label: A
options.text: Population (1971) and area only.

options.label: B
options.text: Demographic performance, tax effort, and forest ecology.

options.label: C
options.text: Per capita income and fiscal discipline only.

options.label: D
options.text: GST compensation cess share and debt ratio.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Demographic performance, tax effort, and forest ecology..

questions.text: Which statement about the 2021 amendment to the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA) is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It made NHRC recommendations legally binding on the government.

options.label: B
options.text: It reduced the tenure of the Chairperson and members to three years, renewable once.

options.label: C
options.text: It removed the requirement for at least one woman member in the NHRC.

options.label: D
options.text: It eliminated the NHRC’s suo motu inquiry powers.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It reduced the tenure of the Chairperson and members to three years, renewable once..

questions.text: In the landmark judgment of Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013), what did the Supreme Court rule regarding Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?

options.label: A
options.text: It upheld Section 8(4) allowing a three-month window for convicted legislators to appeal.

options.label: B
options.text: It struck down Section 8(4), mandating immediate disqualification upon conviction.

options.label: C
options.text: It ruled that disqualification takes effect only after the President's or Governor's formal order.

options.label: D
options.text: It held that the Model Code of Conduct overrides statutory disqualification provisions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It struck down Section 8(4), mandating immediate disqualification upon conviction..

questions.text: What specific procedural mandate was introduced by the 2020 amendment to the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act?

options.label: A
options.text: It made CAG's performance audit reports legally binding on the executive.

options.label: B
options.text: It introduced a six-month timeline for the completion of special audits.

options.label: C
options.text: It removed the CAG's jurisdiction over government companies under the Companies Act, 2013.

options.label: D
options.text: It mandated that all CAG reports be tabled in Parliament within 30 days of submission.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It introduced a six-month timeline for the completion of special audits..

questions.text: Regarding the 103rd Constitutional Amendment providing for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) reservation, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The EWS quota is subject to a creamy layer exclusion similar to the OBC category.

options.label: B
options.text: The amendment explicitly excludes the application of a creamy layer test for EWS.

options.label: C
options.text: The Supreme Court in Janhit Abhiyan struck down the amendment by a 3:2 majority.

options.label: D
options.text: The amendment provides 10% reservation only in public employment, not in educational institutions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The amendment explicitly excludes the application of a creamy layer test for EWS..

questions.text: The 15th Finance Commission (2020-25) introduced new horizontal distribution criteria. Which of the following correctly lists the weights assigned to these criteria?

options.label: A
options.text: Income distance 45%, Forest and ecology 10%, Demographic performance 12.5%, Tax effort 2.5%

options.label: B
options.text: Income distance 50%, Forest and ecology 15%, Demographic performance 10%, Tax effort 5%

options.label: C
options.text: Income distance 40%, Forest and ecology 12.5%, Demographic performance 15%, Tax effort 2.5%

options.label: D
options.text: Income distance 45%, Forest and ecology 12.5%, Demographic performance 10%, Tax effort 5%

questions.solution: Correct answer: Income distance 45%, Forest and ecology 10%, Demographic performance 12.5%, Tax effort 2.5%.

questions.text: What is the status of the GST compensation cess as recommended by the 15th Finance Commission?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a permanent feature of the GST architecture with no sunset clause.

options.label: B
options.text: It is slated to expire in 2026 unless extended by legislation.

options.label: C
options.text: It is levied on all goods and services at a uniform rate of 28%.

options.label: D
options.text: Its proceeds form part of the divisible pool for vertical devolution to States.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It is slated to expire in 2026 unless extended by legislation..

questions.text: Under which constitutional article was the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) established as a constitutional body?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 338

options.label: B
options.text: Article 338A

options.label: C
options.text: Article 338B

options.label: D
options.text: Article 340

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 338B.

questions.text: The removal procedure for a State Election Commissioner is the same as that prescribed for which constitutional functionary?

options.label: A
options.text: Judge of the Supreme Court

options.label: B
options.text: Judge of a High Court

options.label: C
options.text: Chief Election Commissioner

options.label: D
options.text: Governor of the State

questions.solution: Correct answer: Judge of a High Court.

questions.text: From which source do the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) and the Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) derive their authority?

options.label: A
options.text: The Constitution of India

options.label: B
options.text: A statutory enactment

options.label: C
options.text: Parliamentary Rules

options.label: D
options.text: An executive resolution

questions.solution: Correct answer: Parliamentary Rules.

questions.text: The Governor’s power to appoint State‑level constitutional authorities is exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers except in which situation?

options.label: A
options.text: During President’s Rule

options.label: B
options.text: During a State Emergency under Article 356

options.label: C
options.text: When the Legislative Assembly is dissolved

options.label: D
options.text: When the Governor acts in his discretion

questions.solution: Correct answer: During President’s Rule.

questions.text: Which judicial principle was invoked by the Supreme Court to read down the 2018 amendment to the CVC Act that permitted the Government to appoint the Central Vigilance Commissioner without the Leader of Opposition’s concurrence?

options.label: A
options.text: Basic Structure doctrine

options.label: B
options.text: Doctrine of Pleasure

options.label: C
options.text: Principle of Institutional Integrity

options.label: D
options.text: Separation of Powers

questions.solution: Correct answer: Principle of Institutional Integrity.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the consultation requirement for the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) versus the other Election Commissioners (ECs) as interpreted by the Supreme Court in 2015?

options.label: A
options.text: Both CEC and ECs require consultation with the Leader of Opposition (LoP) and the Chief Justice of India (CJI).

options.label: B
options.text: The CEC requires consultation with the LoP and the CJI, while ECs require consultation with the Prime Minister and the LoP only.

options.label: C
options.text: The CEC requires consultation with the CJI only, while ECs require consultation with the LoP only.

options.label: D
options.text: Both CEC and ECs require consultation with the CJI only.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The CEC requires consultation with the LoP and the CJI, while ECs require consultation with the Prime Minister and the LoP only..

questions.text: Which parliamentary committee is specifically tasked with reviewing delegated legislation made by statutory regulators?

options.label: A
options.text: Public Accounts Committee (PAC)

options.label: B
options.text: Committee on Subordinate Legislation

options.label: C
options.text: Estimates Committee

options.label: D
options.text: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table

questions.solution: Correct answer: Committee on Subordinate Legislation.

questions.text: How does the Supreme Court differentiate its standard of review between constitutional bodies (e.g., Election Commission, CAG, UPSC) and statutory bodies (e.g., NHRC, CIC, CVC)?

options.label: A
options.text: It applies the Wednesbury unreasonableness test to constitutional bodies and proportionality to statutory bodies.

options.label: B
options.text: Constitutional bodies receive a higher threshold of judicial deference due to constitutionally entrenched independence, while statutory bodies are subjected to stricter proportionality analysis.

options.label: C
options.text: Both categories are reviewed under the same proportionality standard because all independent bodies must meet identical accountability norms.

options.label: D
options.text: Statutory bodies enjoy higher judicial deference because their enabling statutes provide detailed procedural safeguards.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Constitutional bodies receive a higher threshold of judicial deference due to constitutionally entrenched independence, while statutory bodies are subjected to stricter proportionality analysis..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the composition and statutory origin of the National Commission for Minorities (NCM)?

options.label: A
options.text: A constitutional body under Article 338 with a Chairperson and five members appointed by the President.

options.label: B
options.text: A statutory body constituted under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, comprising a Chairperson, a Vice‑Chairperson and five members appointed by the Central Government.

options.label: C
options.text: A statutory body under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, with a Chairperson and six members, at least two of whom must be women.

options.label: D
options.text: A constitutional body under Article 350B dealing exclusively with linguistic minorities.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A statutory body constituted under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, comprising a Chairperson, a Vice‑Chairperson and five members appointed by the Central Government..

questions.text: What is the legal status of the recommendations made by a State Finance Commission (SFC) to the State Government?

options.label: A
options.text: They are binding on the State Government and must be implemented without legislative approval.

options.label: B
options.text: They are advisory in nature and require acceptance by the State Legislature before implementation.

options.label: C
options.text: They are binding only with respect to devolution to Panchayats, but advisory for Municipalities.

options.label: D
options.text: They are binding only for Municipalities, while Panchayats receive advisory recommendations.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They are advisory in nature and require acceptance by the State Legislature before implementation..

questions.text: Which statement correctly characterises the role of the Inter‑State Council under Article 263 of the Constitution?

options.label: A
options.text: It functions as a dispute‑resolution body whose orders are binding on the States.

options.label: B
options.text: It is an advisory body tasked with inquiring into and advising upon disputes between States.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a statutory body established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

options.label: D
options.text: It possesses legislative powers to make laws on subjects in the State List.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It is an advisory body tasked with inquiring into and advising upon disputes between States..

questions.text: From which source does the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) derive its mandate to conduct performance audits?

options.label: A
options.text: Explicit provisions in the Constitution of India.

options.label: B
options.text: The CAG Act, 1971 and executive practice.

options.label: C
options.text: Recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission.

options.label: D
options.text: Guidelines issued under the Outcome Budgeting framework.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The CAG Act, 1971 and executive practice..

questions.text: Following the Right to Information (Amendment) Act, 2019 and subsequent Supreme Court judgments, what is the current position regarding the tenure and salary of the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) and Information Commissioners (ICs)?

options.label: A
options.text: The original five‑year tenure and salary parity with the Chief Election Commissioner/Election Commissioners remain unchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: The 2020 Rules fixed a three‑year tenure and Secretary‑level pay, but the Supreme Court directed restoration of the pre‑2019 tenure and salary structure.

options.label: C
options.text: The 2019 Amendment permanently fixed a three‑year tenure with Secretary‑level pay, and the Supreme Court upheld it.

options.label: D
options.text: Tenure and salary are now determined by respective State Governments for State Information Commissions only.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The 2020 Rules fixed a three‑year tenure and Secretary‑level pay, but the Supreme Court directed restoration of the pre‑2019 tenure and salary structure..

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the removal process of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) as per the Constitution and subsequent judicial pronouncements?

options.label: A
options.text: CEC can be removed by President on recommendation of Prime Minister after a parliamentary committee finds serious breach of conduct.

options.label: B
options.text: CEC can be removed only on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity by a resolution passed by each House of Parliament with special majority.

options.label: C
options.text: CEC can be removed by a simple majority resolution in Lok Sabha only.

options.label: D
options.text: CEC can be removed by the Supreme Court on a petition of misconduct.

questions.solution: Correct answer: CEC can be removed only on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity by a resolution passed by each House of Parliament with special majority..

questions.text: What is the constitutional basis of the Inter‑State Council (ISC) and how does it differ from the Zonal Councils?

options.label: A
options.text: Both ISC and Zonal Councils are constitutional bodies under Article 263.

options.label: B
options.text: ISC is a constitutional body under Article 263, whereas Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

options.label: C
options.text: ISC is a statutory body under the Inter‑State Council Act, 1990, while Zonal Councils are constitutional.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither ISC nor Zonal Councils have any constitutional or statutory basis.

questions.solution: Correct answer: ISC is a constitutional body under Article 263, whereas Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956..

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the constitutional status and advisory role of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) after the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018?

options.label: A
options.text: The NCBC became a constitutional body under Article 338B and its recommendations are binding on both the Central and State Governments.

options.label: B
options.text: The NCBC acquired constitutional status under Article 338B, but its recommendations bind only the Central Government for the Central List of OBCs.

options.label: C
options.text: The NCBC remains a statutory body under the 1993 Act, with the 102nd Amendment only extending its tenure to three years.

options.label: D
options.text: The President's notification under Article 338B empowers the NCBC to prepare State Lists of OBCs, overriding State Backward Classes Commissions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The NCBC acquired constitutional status under Article 338B, but its recommendations bind only the Central Government for the Central List of OBCs..

questions.text: According to the Supreme Court's interpretation in Vineet Narain and Common Cause cases, what is the nature of the Central Vigilance Commission's (CVC) superintendence over the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)?

options.label: A
options.text: The CVC's superintendence is merely advisory and the CBI is not obligated to follow its directions.

options.label: B
options.text: The CVC exercises binding superintendence over the CBI in matters relating to investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

options.label: C
options.text: The CVC has administrative control over the CBI, including transfers and postings of its officers.

options.label: D
options.text: The CVC's role is limited to reviewing the CBI's annual reports and it cannot interfere in ongoing investigations.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The CVC exercises binding superintendence over the CBI in matters relating to investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act..

questions.text: The Inter‑State Council, constituted under Article 263 by the Constitution (Inter‑State Council) Act, 1990, is chaired by which Union Minister and includes which members?

options.label: A
options.text: Union Finance Minister; Chief Ministers of all states and Lt Governors of UTs

options.label: B
options.text: Union Home Minister; Chief Ministers of all states and Lt Governors of UTs

options.label: C
options.text: Union Home Minister; only Chief Ministers of states

options.label: D
options.text: Prime Minister; Chief Ministers and Lt Governors

questions.solution: Correct answer: Union Home Minister; Chief Ministers of all states and Lt Governors of UTs.

questions.text: The Supreme Court's judgment in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) primarily dealt with which constitutional provision and what was its key holding?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 356; President's Rule can be imposed only on objective material and is subject to judicial review.

options.label: B
options.text: Article 254; Union law prevails over State law on Concurrent subjects.

options.label: C
options.text: Article 263; Inter‑State Council's recommendations are binding.

options.label: D
options.text: Article 371; Special provisions for certain states are unconstitutional.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 356; President's Rule can be imposed only on objective material and is subject to judicial review..

questions.text: In the 15th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution formula, what is the weight assigned to income distance?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 45%.

questions.text: What is the voting weight distribution between the Centre and the states in the GST Council?

options.label: A
options.text: Centre 1/2, states 1/2

options.label: B
options.text: Centre 1/3, states 2/3

options.label: C
options.text: Centre 2/3, states 1/3

options.label: D
options.text: Centre 1/4, states 3/4

questions.solution: Correct answer: Centre 1/3, states 2/3.

questions.text: Local-body grants recommended by the Finance Commission are conditional upon:

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Recommendations of the respective State Finance Commission

options.label: C
options.text: Approval by the GST Council

options.label: D
options.text: A resolution of the State Legislative Assembly

questions.solution: Correct answer: Recommendations of the respective State Finance Commission.

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the Supreme Court's power of review over awards of Inter-State River Water Disputes Tribunals under Article 262?

options.label: A
options.text: The Supreme Court has no jurisdiction whatsoever

options.label: B
options.text: The Supreme Court can review awards only on grounds of jurisdictional error or violation of fundamental rights

options.label: C
options.text: The Supreme Court can hear appeals as a matter of right

options.text: The Supreme Court can review awards only if both states consent

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court can review awards only on grounds of jurisdictional error or violation of fundamental rights.

questions.text: In the case of K. C. G. Narayanan v. State of Kerala (1965), the Supreme Court struck down a state law on the ground of:

options.label: A
options.text: Pith and substance

options.label: B
options.text: Colourable legislation

options.label: C
options.text: Repugnancy

questions.solution: Correct answer: Colourable legislation.

questions.text: In the context of the S.R. Bommai (1994) and Government of NCT of Delhi (2021) judgments, which of the following statements correctly describes the judicial safeguards for federalism?

options.label: A
options.text: The Bommai judgment made the President's satisfaction under Article 356 immune from judicial review on the ground of political expediency.

options.label: B
options.text: The NCT of Delhi judgment held that the Lieutenant Governor's concurrence is required on all matters within the legislative competence of the Delhi Assembly.

options.label: C
options.text: The Bommai guidelines mandate a floor test in the state assembly before dissolution and require the Centre to place the material for President's satisfaction before Parliament.

options.label: D
options.text: The basic structure doctrine was held inapplicable to federalism in Bommai, limiting it only to supremacy of the Constitution and separation of powers.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Bommai guidelines mandate a floor test in the state assembly before dissolution and require the Centre to place the material for President's satisfaction before Parliament..

questions.text: Regarding the flexi-fund mechanism under Centrally Sponsored Schemes as revised by the 15th Finance Commission (2021-26), which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: States can re-allocate up to 25% of each CSS allocation to any state-specific scheme without sectoral restrictions.

options.label: B
options.text: The 25% flexi-fund ceiling applies scheme-wise, and re-allocated funds must remain within the broad sectoral objectives of the respective CSS.

options.label: C
options.text: The flexi-fund mechanism was introduced by the 14th Finance Commission and made statutory through an Act of Parliament.

options.label: D
options.text: States require prior Union Cabinet approval for each flexi-fund utilisation plan submitted to the line ministry.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The 25% flexi-fund ceiling applies scheme-wise, and re-allocated funds must remain within the broad sectoral objectives of the respective CSS..

questions.text: With reference to the National Data Governance Framework Policy (NDGFP) and digital federalism, which of the following is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The NDGFP is an enacted statute providing a legally enforceable framework for mandatory inter-state data sharing.

options.label: B
options.text: The NDGFP is a draft executive policy that currently lacks statutory enforceability and does not mandate inter-state data sharing.

options.label: C
options.text: The NDGFP establishes a centralised data repository under the exclusive control of the Union Government for all state-generated data.

options.label: D
options.text: The NDGFP has been ratified by the Inter-State Council and thus binds all states under Article 263.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The NDGFP is a draft executive policy that currently lacks statutory enforceability and does not mandate inter-state data sharing..

questions.text: Concerning the 101st Constitutional Amendment (GST) and the compensation regime, which statement is correct based on the State of Kerala v. Union of India (2023) judgment?

options.label: A
options.text: The Supreme Court held that the GST compensation cess must continue beyond five years as it is a constitutional guarantee under Article 279A.

options.label: B
options.text: The Supreme Court upheld the Union's discretion to discontinue the compensation cess after the five-year constitutional period (June 2022), as the guarantee was statutory, not constitutional.

options.label: C
options.text: The GST Council's recommendations become binding on the Union and states immediately upon passage, without requiring Presidential assent.

options.label: D
options.text: States retain independent rate-setting power on all subsumed taxes through their representation in the GST Council.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court upheld the Union's discretion to discontinue the compensation cess after the five-year constitutional period (June 2022), as the guarantee was statutory, not constitutional..

questions.text: In the context of the Inter-State Council's role in water disputes, which of the following accurately describes its function and outcomes in the Cauvery, Krishna, and Mahadayi cases?

options.label: A
options.text: The ISC acts as a binding adjudicatory body under Article 262, and its decisions in Cauvery and Krishna disputes overrode the respective Tribunal awards.

options.text: The ISC's recommendations in the Cauvery dispute led to the constitution of the Cauvery Water Management Authority and Regulation Committee, illustrating its role as a political facilitator.

options.label: C
options.text: The ISC successfully constituted the Mahadayi River Basin Authority in 2021, which is now fully operational for implementing the Tribunal's award.

options.label: D
options.text: The ISC meetings on Krishna and Mahadayi disputes were attended by all Chief Ministers and resulted in immediate implementation of Tribunal awards without further negotiation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The ISC's recommendations in the Cauvery dispute led to the constitution of the Cauvery Water Management Authority and Regulation Committee, illustrating its role as a political facilitator..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes a change in horizontal devolution criteria from the 14th to the 15th Finance Commission?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Income distance weight reduced from 50% to 45% and tax effort introduced at 2.5%

options.label: C
options.text: Forest cover weight reduced from 10% to 7.5% and demographic performance removed

options.label: D
options.text: Area weight increased from 15% to 20% and 2011 Census replaced by 2021 Census

questions.solution: Correct answer: Income distance weight reduced from 50% to 45% and tax effort introduced at 2.5%.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately distinguishes the NITI Aayog Governing Council from the National Development Council (NDC)?

options.text: The NITI Aayog Governing Council allocates plan outlays to states, while the NDC only approved five-year plans

options.label: B
options.text: The NITI Aayog Governing Council includes Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories with legislatures, which the NDC did not

options.label: C
options.text: The NDC was chaired by the Finance Minister, whereas the NITI Aayog Governing Council is chaired by the Prime Minister

options.label: D
options.text: The NDC formulated strategic policy frameworks, while NITI Aayog focuses solely on financial resource allocation

questions.solution: Correct answer: The NITI Aayog Governing Council includes Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories with legislatures, which the NDC did not.

questions.text: Under Article 304 of the Constitution, as interpreted in the context of GST, what restriction applies to state taxation powers on inter-state goods?

options.label: A
options.text: States may levy any tax on inter-state goods provided it is non-discriminatory

options.label: B
options.text: States may impose non-discriminatory restrictions only on goods not subsumed under GST

options.label: C
options.text: States are prohibited from imposing any restriction on inter-state trade after GST

options.label: D
options.text: States require prior Presidential assent for all taxes on inter-state goods

questions.solution: Correct answer: States may impose non-discriminatory restrictions only on goods not subsumed under GST.

questions.text: According to the 15th Finance Commission's design for performance-based grants, what proportion of the health grant is released as unconditional base allocation?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 60%.

questions.text: What is the Centre-State funding ratio for State Disaster Response Funds (SDRFs) for general category states as per the Disaster Management Act framework?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 75:25.

questions.text: Under Article 249 of the Constitution, a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha to empower Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest must be supported by what majority and remains in force for what initial period?

options.label: A
options.text: Simple majority of total membership; six months

options.label: B
options.text: Two-thirds of members present and voting; one year

options.label: C
options.text: Two-thirds of total membership; one year

options.label: D
options.text: Simple majority of members present and voting; one year

questions.solution: Correct answer: Two-thirds of members present and voting; one year.

questions.text: Article 257 of the Constitution authorises the Union to give directions to a State in which of the following specific matters?

options.label: A
options.text: Regulation of inter-state trade and commerce

options.label: B
options.text: Construction or maintenance of means of communication of national or military importance

options.label: C
options.text: Imposition of President's Rule in case of constitutional breakdown

options.label: D
options.text: Allocation of financial resources from the Consolidated Fund of India

questions.solution: Correct answer: Construction or maintenance of means of communication of national or military importance.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the nature of the Union's obligation under Article 355 of the Constitution?

options.label: A
options.text: It confers a discretionary power on the Union to intervene in State administration at will.

options.label: B
options.text: It imposes a constitutional duty on the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance.

options.label: C
options.text: It allows the Union to supersede the executive authority of a State without a Proclamation of Emergency.

options.label: D
options.text: It is applicable only when a Proclamation of Financial Emergency under Article 360 is in operation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It imposes a constitutional duty on the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance..

questions.text: The voting structure of the GST Council, as constituted under Article 279A, provides for which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: The Union holds 50% voting weight and decisions are taken by simple majority.

options.label: B
options.text: The Union holds one-third voting weight, States collectively hold two-thirds, and resolutions require a three-fourths weighted majority if consensus fails.

options.label: C
options.text: Each State's voting weight is proportional to its population and revenue contribution.

options.label: D
options.text: Disputes are finally resolved by a dedicated GST Appellate Tribunal constituted under the GST Act.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Union holds one-third voting weight, States collectively hold two-thirds, and resolutions require a three-fourths weighted majority if consensus fails..

questions.text: With reference to Article 200 of the Constitution and the Governor's power to reserve State Bills for Presidential consideration, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The Governor possesses absolute discretion to reserve any Bill passed by the State Legislature for the President's assent.

options.label: B
options.text: Once the President gives assent to a reserved Bill, it becomes a Union law applicable to the entire territory of India.

options.label: C
options.text: The Supreme Court in Nabam Rebia (2016) limited the Governor's discretion to reserve Bills only to cases involving constitutional grounds.

options.label: D
options.text: The President is bound to give assent to a Bill reserved by the Governor under Article 200.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court in Nabam Rebia (2016) limited the Governor's discretion to reserve Bills only to cases involving constitutional grounds..

questions.text: The 14th Finance Commission recommended a vertical devolution of 42 per cent of the divisible pool to States. In this context, which of the following components of Union revenue is explicitly excluded from the divisible pool for the purpose of vertical devolution?

options.label: A
options.text: Corporation Tax

options.label: B
options.text: Income Tax

options.label: C
options.text: Cesses and Surcharges

options.label: D
options.text: Customs Duties

questions.solution: Correct answer: Cesses and Surcharges.

questions.text: The GST (Compensation to States) Amendment Act, 2022 extended the levy of the compensation cess until March 2026. What was the primary rationale for this extension as decided by the GST Council in its 47th meeting (June 2022)?

options.label: A
options.text: To continue guaranteeing States a 14 per cent annual growth in GST revenue beyond the original five-year transition period.

options.label: B
options.text: To repay the borrowings undertaken by the Centre in 2020-21 and 2021-22 to meet compensation shortfalls and to clear residual arrears.

options.label: C
options.text: To expand the basket of goods subject to the cess to include electric vehicles and other green mobility products.

options.label: D
options.text: To increase the voting weight of the Union Government in the GST Council from one-third to one-half for cess-related decisions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: To repay the borrowings undertaken by the Centre in 2020-21 and 2021-22 to meet compensation shortfalls and to clear residual arrears..

questions.text: Under Article 3 of the Constitution, what is the legal effect of the views expressed by the Legislature of an affected State on a reorganisation Bill?

options.label: A
options.text: The State Legislature's consent is mandatory before Parliament can pass the Bill.

options.label: B
options.text: The President may disregard the State Legislature's views only if a special majority is obtained in Parliament.

options.label: C
options.text: The State Legislature's opinion is advisory; Parliament may proceed after the prescribed period expires or after receiving the views.

options.label: D
options.text: The Bill must be referred to the State Legislature only if the reorganisation involves a change of name.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The State Legislature's opinion is advisory; Parliament may proceed after the prescribed period expires or after receiving the views..

questions.text: Why was the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Bill, 2019 not referred to the State Legislature for its views before introduction in Parliament?

options.label: A
options.text: Jammu and Kashmir had no Legislative Assembly at the time.

options.label: B
options.text: The State was under President's Rule under Article 356, allowing the President to dispense with the referral requirement.

options.label: C
options.text: Article 3 does not require State consultation for the creation of Union Territories.

options.label: D
options.text: The Bill was introduced as a Constitutional Amendment requiring a special majority.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The State was under President's Rule under Article 356, allowing the President to dispense with the referral requirement..

questions.text: Which Supreme Court case laid down the "instrumentality test" to determine whether a body qualifies as "State" under Article 12 of the Constitution?

options.label: A
options.text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala

options.label: B
options.text: R. D. Shetty v. Airport Authority of India

options.label: C
options.text: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India

options.label: D
options.text: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation

questions.solution: Correct answer: R. D. Shetty v. Airport Authority of India.

questions.text: The Directive Principles of State Policy are classified in the constitutional scheme into which three categories?

options.label: A
options.text: Civil, Political, Socio‑economic

options.label: B
options.text: Socialistic, Gandhian, Liberal‑Intellectual

options.label: C
options.text: Justiciable, Non‑justiciable, Moral

options.label: D
options.text: Fundamental, Derivative, Ancillary

questions.solution: Correct answer: Socialistic, Gandhian, Liberal‑Intellectual.

questions.text: Which constitutional amendment inserted the Fundamental Duties and which later amendment added the duty to provide opportunities for education to children between six and fourteen years?

options.label: A
options.text: 42nd Amendment inserted duties; 86th Amendment added education duty

options.label: B
options.text: 44th Amendment inserted duties; 86th Amendment added education duty

options.label: C
options.text: 42nd Amendment inserted duties; 91st Amendment added education duty

options.label: D
options.text: 44th Amendment inserted duties; 91st Amendment added education duty

questions.solution: Correct answer: 42nd Amendment inserted duties; 86th Amendment added education duty.

questions.text: The doctrine of harmonious construction, holding that the amending power under Article 368 cannot destroy the basic structure including the balance between Parts III and IV, was notably affirmed in which landmark case?

options.label: A
options.text: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India

options.label: B
options.text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala

options.label: C
options.text: Golak Nath v. State of Punjab

options.label: D
options.text: State of Karnataka v. Ranganatha Reddy

questions.solution: Correct answer: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala.

questions.text: The shift from the "procedure established by law" doctrine in A.K. Gopalan to the "due process" interpretation in Maneka Gandhi primarily expanded the scope of which Fundamental Right?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 14 (Equality)

options.label: B
options.text: Article 19 (Freedom)

options.label: C
options.text: Article 21 (Life and Personal Liberty)

options.label: D
options.text: Article 22 (Protection against arrest)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 21 (Life and Personal Liberty).

questions.text: With reference to the Doctrine of Eclipse under Article 13, consider the following statements: 1. A pre-constitutional law inconsistent with Fundamental Rights becomes void ab initio. 2. Such a law revives automatically if the conflicting constitutional provision is amended. 3. The doctrine applies equally to post-constitutional laws. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 only

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 3 only

options.label: D
options.text: 1, 2 and 3

questions.solution: Correct answer: 2 only.

questions.text: In Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978), the Supreme Court transformed Article 21 by interpreting 'procedure established by law' as requiring the procedure to be:

options.label: A
options.text: Enacted by a competent legislature only

options.label: B
options.text: Fair, just and reasonable

options.label: C
options.text: Consistent with Article 19 only

options.label: D
options.text: Approved by the President

questions.solution: Correct answer: Fair, just and reasonable.

questions.text: Article 31C, as originally enacted by the 25th Amendment (1971), protected laws giving effect to which Directive Principles from challenge under Articles 14 and 19?

options.label: A
options.text: Articles 39(b) and 39(c) only

options.label: B
options.text: All Directive Principles in Part IV

options.label: C
options.text: Articles 38, 39, 41 and 48A only

options.label: D
options.text: Articles 39(a) and 39(b) only

questions.solution: Correct answer: Articles 39(b) and 39(c) only.

questions.text: According to the 'dual test' laid down in I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007), a law placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 is:

options.label: A
options.text: Immune from judicial review entirely

options.label: B
options.text: Subject to judicial review only if it violates Article 21

options.label: C
options.text: Subject to judicial review if it violates the basic structure

options.label: D
options.text: Valid only if ratified by half the State Legislatures

questions.solution: Correct answer: Subject to judicial review if it violates the basic structure.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the current legal status of Fundamental Duties under Article 51A?

options.label: A
options.text: They are justiciable and directly enforceable by courts

options.label: B
options.text: They are purely moral exhortations with no legal effect

options.label: C
options.text: They are non-justiciable but have acquired legal traction through statutes and judicial interpretation

options.label: D
options.text: They are enforceable only through constitutional writs under Article 32

questions.solution: Correct answer: They are non-justiciable but have acquired legal traction through statutes and judicial interpretation.

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the "reasonable classification" test and the "manifest arbitrariness" test under Article 14 as per the Supreme Court?

options.label: A
options.text: Manifest arbitrariness replaces the reasonable classification test entirely.

options.label: B
options.text: The reasonable classification test is applied only when manifest arbitrariness fails.

options.label: C
options.text: Manifest arbitrariness supplements the reasonable classification test; a law may pass classification but still fail manifest arbitrariness.

options.label: D
options.text: Both tests are mutually exclusive and cannot be applied together.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Manifest arbitrariness supplements the reasonable classification test; a law may pass classification but still fail manifest arbitrariness..

questions.text: On what primary ground did the Supreme Court declare Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 unconstitutional in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)?

options.label: A
options.text: Violation of the right to equality under Article 14.

options.label: B
options.text: Violation of the right to privacy under Article 21.

options.label: C
options.text: Being vague and overbroad, thereby violating freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a).

options.label: D
options.text: Exceeding the legislative competence of Parliament.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Being vague and overbroad, thereby violating freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a)..

questions.text: Which of the following accurately reflects the scope of the right guaranteed under Article 21A of the Constitution?

options.label: A
options.text: It guarantees quality education outcomes for every child aged 6‑14 years.

options.label: B
options.text: It guarantees free and compulsory access to education for children aged 6‑14 years, not outcomes.

options.label: C
options.text: It applies only to private unaided schools receiving no state aid.

options.label: D
options.text: It is enforceable only through executive orders and not subject to judicial review.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It guarantees free and compulsory access to education for children aged 6‑14 years, not outcomes..

questions.text: In the context of Public Interest Litigation and the doctrine of prospective overruling, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: A PIL can be filed without demonstrating the absence of an alternative remedy.

options.label: B
options.text: Prospective overruling automatically shields all past actions from a declaration of unconstitutionality.

options.label: C
options.text: The Supreme Court in S.P. Gupta laid down that a PIL petitioner must act bona fide, involve substantial public interest, and show no alternative remedy.

options.label: D
options.text: Prospective overruling is a substantive right available to any litigant.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court in S.P. Gupta laid down that a PIL petitioner must act bona fide, involve substantial public interest, and show no alternative remedy..

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the 103rd Constitutional Amendment (2019) and the Supreme Court's ruling in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022)?

options.label: A
options.text: It provides 10% reservation for EWS subject to the creamy layer and the 50% ceiling applies.

options.label: B
options.text: It provides 10% reservation for EWS without creamy layer but the 50% ceiling applies.

options.label: C
options.text: It provides 10% reservation for EWS without creamy layer and the 50% ceiling does not apply to economic criteria.

options.label: D
options.text: It provides 10% reservation for EWS only in State‑aided institutions and the creamy layer test applies.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It provides 10% reservation for EWS without creamy layer and the 50% ceiling does not apply to economic criteria..

questions.text: Article 16(4B) of the Constitution, inserted by the 81st Amendment (2000), permits the State to:

options.label: A
options.text: Provide reservation in promotions for SCs and STs with consequential seniority.

options.label: B
options.text: Carry forward unfilled reserved vacancies to subsequent years without breaching the 50% ceiling.

options.label: C
options.text: Extend reservation to economically weaker sections in public employment.

options.label: D
options.text: Remove the creamy layer exclusion for OBCs in promotions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Carry forward unfilled reserved vacancies to subsequent years without breaching the 50% ceiling..

questions.text: Regarding Article 300A (Right to Property), which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a fundamental right enforceable directly under Article 32 of the Constitution.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a constitutional right but not a fundamental right; remedies lie under Article 226.

options.label: C
options.text: It was inserted by the 44th Amendment and restores the pre‑1978 fundamental right to property.

options.label: D
options.text: It grants an absolute, non‑derogable right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It is a constitutional right but not a fundamental right; remedies lie under Article 226..

questions.text: In which case did the Supreme Court apply the doctrine of proportionality to uphold a ban on gutkha under Article 19(1)(g) read with Article 19(6)?

options.label: A
options.text: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)

options.label: B
options.text: Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007)

options.label: C
options.text: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022)

options.label: D
options.text: Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007).

questions.text: What was the principal holding of the Supreme Court in Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980) concerning the 42nd Amendment?

options.label: A
options.text: It upheld the amendment giving Directive Principles primacy over Fundamental Rights.

options.label: B
options.text: It struck down the provisions that sought to make Directive Principles immune from judicial scrutiny.

options.label: C
options.text: It declared all Directive Principles justiciable and enforceable by courts.

options.label: D
options.text: It expanded the protective scope of Article 31C to all socio‑economic legislation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It struck down the provisions that sought to make Directive Principles immune from judicial scrutiny..

questions.text: In the evolution of the right to privacy under Article 21, which of the following statements accurately describes the contribution of the Govind v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1975) judgment?

options.label: A
options.text: It unanimously declared privacy a fundamental right intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21.

options.label: B
options.text: It held that 'personal liberty' did not include a right to privacy, upholding police surveillance regulations.

options.label: C
options.text: It accepted that privacy could be inferred from Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(d) and 21, but subjected it to 'reasonable restrictions' on grounds of public order.

options.label: D
options.text: It identified three core aspects of privacy: bodily integrity, informational self-determination, and decisional autonomy.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It accepted that privacy could be inferred from Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(d) and 21, but subjected it to 'reasonable restrictions' on grounds of public order..

questions.text: Regarding judicial interpretation of Article 19(1)(g), which of the following distinctions has the Supreme Court consistently maintained while evaluating state restrictions?

options.label: A
options.text: The distinction between 'regulation' (which preserves the essence of the right) and 'prohibition' (which extinguishes it).

options.label: B
options.text: The distinction between 'reasonable restrictions' under Article 19(6) and 'procedure established by law' under Article 21.

options.label: C
options.text: The distinction between 'economic liberty' as a fundamental right and 'Directive Principles' as non-justiciable guidelines.

options.label: D
options.text: The distinction between 'professional autonomy' to set fees and 'statutory conditions' under the Industrial Disputes Act.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The distinction between 'regulation' (which preserves the essence of the right) and 'prohibition' (which extinguishes it)..

questions.text: Under the TMA Pai framework for Article 30(1), which of the following is a necessary condition for an institution to claim minority status and administrative autonomy?

options.label: A
options.text: The institution must be affiliated to a state university and receive state aid.

options.label: B
options.text: The institution must be established by the minority community and serve its interests.

options.label: C
options.text: The institution must reserve 25% seats for economically weaker sections under the RTE Act.

options.label: D
options.text: The institution must be administered by a religious denomination registered under the Societies Registration Act.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The institution must be established by the minority community and serve its interests..

questions.text: The requirement that the "procedure established by law" under Article 21 must be "fair, just and reasonable" was introduced in which case?

options.label: A
options.text: K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950)

options.label: B
options.text: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)

options.label: C
options.text: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)

options.label: D
options.text: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978).

questions.text: After the Minerva Mills judgment, Article 31C protects only which Directive Principles?

options.label: A
options.text: All Directive Principles of State Policy

options.label: B
options.text: Only Article 39(b) and (c)

options.label: C
options.text: Only Article 48A and Article 51A(g)

options.label: D
options.text: Only the Directive Principles inserted by the 42nd Amendment

questions.solution: Correct answer: Only Article 39(b) and (c).

questions.text: How have Indian courts used Fundamental Duties in judicial reasoning?

options.label: A
options.text: As directly enforceable rights through writ petitions

options.label: B
options.text: As mere moral exhortations with no legal relevance

options.label: C
options.text: As interpretive aids to construe statutes and Fundamental Rights and as guides for legislation

options.label: D
options.text: As provisions that override Fundamental Rights in case of conflict

questions.solution: Correct answer: As interpretive aids to construe statutes and Fundamental Rights and as guides for legislation.

questions.text: The "triple test" mandated by the Supreme Court for any state intrusion into personal data or restriction of internet access consists of:

options.label: A
options.text: Legality, necessity, proportionality

options.label: B
options.text: Reasonableness, fairness, transparency

options.label: C
options.text: Consent, purpose limitation, data minimisation

options.label: D
options.text: State interest, public order, morality

questions.solution: Correct answer: Legality, necessity, proportionality.

questions.text: Which case first articulated the principle of colourable legislation in Indian constitutional law?

options.label: A
options.text: K. C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa (1953)

options.label: B
options.text: State of Bihar v. Kameshwar Singh (1952)

options.label: C
options.text: R. C. Cooper v. Union of India (1970)

options.label: D
options.text: K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)

questions.solution: Correct answer: K. C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa (1953).

questions.text: In which case was the doctrine of pith and substance crystallised for resolving overlaps between Union and State legislative entries?

options.label: A
options.text: State of Bombay v. F. N. Balsara (1951)

options.label: B
options.text: K. C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa (1953)

options.label: C
options.text: Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)

options.label: D
options.text: S. P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981)

questions.solution: Correct answer: State of Bombay v. F. N. Balsara (1951).

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the legal status of recommendations made by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)?

options.label: A
options.text: They are binding on the government and enforceable by writ.

options.label: B
options.text: They are persuasive but not enforceable by writ.

options.label: C
options.text: They have the force of law under Article 32.

options.label: D
options.text: They are automatically incorporated into judicial orders.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They are persuasive but not enforceable by writ..

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the constitutional basis of the Right to Information in India as established by the Supreme Court in State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain (1975)?

options.label: A
options.text: The Court declared Right to Information as an independent fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution.

options.label: B
options.text: The Court held that the right to know is an intrinsic facet of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a), subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).

options.label: C
options.text: The Court ruled that the Official Secrets Act, 1923, was unconstitutional as it violated the citizens' right to information.

options.label: D
options.text: The Court mandated the immediate enactment of a comprehensive Right to Information legislation within six months.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Court held that the right to know is an intrinsic facet of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a), subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2)..

questions.text: What is the role of the CPGRAMS portal in India's multi-tier grievance redress architecture?

options.label: A
options.text: It serves as the exclusive platform for filing complaints under the Right to Information Act, 2005.

options.label: B
options.text: It integrates the three tiers of grievance redress by allowing citizens to file complaints, track escalation, and receive final orders.

options.label: C
options.text: It functions as the primary interface for the Lokpal to receive complaints against the Prime Minister and other public servants.

options.label: D
options.text: It replaces the departmental-level grievance officers and directly connects citizens to the Central Vigilance Commission.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It integrates the three tiers of grievance redress by allowing citizens to file complaints, track escalation, and receive final orders..

questions.text: Which of the following reforms was introduced by the "Mission Karmayogi" programme launched in 2019?

options.label: A
options.text: Mandatory cooling-off period of two years for civil servants moving to regulatory bodies after retirement.

options.label: B
options.text: Lateral entry of private sector professionals at the level of Joint Secretary in central ministries.

options.label: C
options.text: Institutionalisation of continuous capacity building through a competency framework for civil servants.

options.label: D
options.text: Redesign of the Performance Appraisal Report to include 360-degree feedback and key result areas.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Institutionalisation of continuous capacity building through a competency framework for civil servants..

questions.text: Under Section 8(2) of the RTI Act, 2005, the public‑interest override operates as:

options.label: A
options.text: A discretionary power of the Public Information Officer to decide whether to disclose exempted information.

options.label: B
options.text: A mandatory requirement to disclose information once the public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interest.

options.label: C
options.text: A provision that applies only to intelligence and security organisations listed in the Second Schedule.

options.label: D
options.text: A rule that allows the Central Information Commission to override exemptions on its own motion.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A mandatory requirement to disclose information once the public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interest..

questions.text: Which Supreme Court judgment held that evaluated answer scripts constitute "information" under the RTI Act and cannot be withheld under the fiduciary‑relationship exemption (Section 8(1)(e))?

options.label: A
options.text: Namit Sharma v. Union of India (2013)

options.label: B
options.text: Reserve Bank of India v. Jayantilal Mistry (2016)

options.label: C
options.text: Central Board of Secondary Education v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)

options.label: D
options.text: Anjali Bhardwaj v. Union of India (2019)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Central Board of Secondary Education v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011).

questions.text: According to the 2019 CIC audit of 2,500 central ministries and departments, which of the following was NOT identified as a common compliance gap in proactive disclosure under Section 4(1)(b)?

options.label: A
options.text: Absence of updated decision‑making flowcharts

options.label: B
options.text: Non‑publication of subsidy beneficiary lists

options.label: C
options.text: Lack of machine‑readable datasets

options.label: D
options.text: Absence of organisational structure and powers of officers

questions.solution: Correct answer: Absence of organisational structure and powers of officers.

questions.text: In the redesigned Performance Appraisal Report (PAR) under Mission Karmayogi, what is the weightage assigned to Behavioural Competencies?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 30%.

questions.text: Which of the following changes were introduced by the Whistle Blowers Protection (Amendment) Act, 2015?

options.label: A
options.text: Expanded the definition of victimisation to include routine transfers and denial of promotion.

options.label: B
options.text: Narrowed the definition of victimisation and added a broad exemption for disclosures affecting national security, public order, or friendly relations with foreign states.

options.label: C
options.text: Removed the confidentiality requirement for the complainant's identity.

options.label: D
options.text: Extended statutory protection to private‑sector employees in public‑private partnerships.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Narrowed the definition of victimisation and added a broad exemption for disclosures affecting national security, public order, or friendly relations with foreign states..

questions.text: Under State Public Service Guarantee Acts, what is the consequence if the designated authority fails to deliver the notified service within the stipulated timeline?

options.label: A
options.text: The applicant must submit a fresh application after the timeline expires.

options.label: B
options.text: The service is deemed approved automatically on expiry of the notified timeline.

options.label: C
options.text: The authority may extend the timeline at its discretion without any legal consequence.

options.label: D
options.text: The applicant can directly approach the Lokpal for redressal.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The service is deemed approved automatically on expiry of the notified timeline..

questions.text: Which statement accurately reflects the licensing status of datasets published on the Open Government Data Platform (data.gov.in)?

options.label: A

questions.text: Regarding the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) mechanism of the UN Human Rights Council, which of the following statements is correct?

questions.text: Concerning the International Health Regulations (IHR) 2005 and their amendment process, which statement is correct?

questions.text: Regarding the Loss and Damage Fund established at COP27 and operationalized at COP28, which statement is correct?

questions.text: Which statement correctly characterises the IMF’s Resilience and Sustainability Trust (RST)?

questions.text: Regarding the G20 Anti‑Corruption Working Group’s 2023 High‑Level Principles on Beneficial Ownership Transparency, which of the following is true?

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the status and function of 'soft law' instruments, such as UN General Assembly resolutions, in the international legal system?

questions.text: Referring to the Supreme Court's observation in Divisional Manager, Aravali Golf Club v. Chander Hass (2008), which principle of judicial conduct was emphasised to counter the risks of judicial activism?
