options.text: It was applied in Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala (2018) to defer the enforcement of the right to equality.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court must expressly state that its ruling shall have prospective effect; silence implies retrospective application..

questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes 'constitutional morality' from 'popular morality' as interpreted by the Supreme Court?

options.label: A
options.text: Constitutional morality is derived from prevailing social norms, while popular morality is anchored in the constitutional text.

options.label: B
options.text: Constitutional morality is anchored in the constitutional text and transformative vision, whereas popular morality shifts with social majorities.

options.label: C
options.text: Constitutional morality applies only to fundamental rights adjudication, while popular morality governs directive principles.

options.label: D
options.text: Constitutional morality is determined by parliamentary legislation, while popular morality is determined by judicial precedent.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Constitutional morality is anchored in the constitutional text and transformative vision, whereas popular morality shifts with social majorities..

questions.text: Regarding judicial review of ordinances under Article 123 and Article 213, what is the correct position as per Supreme Court jurisprudence?

options.label: A
options.text: The President's or Governor's satisfaction for promulgating an ordinance is entirely non-justiciable and immune from judicial scrutiny.

options.label: B
options.text: The satisfaction is justiciable only on the ground of mala fides, but not on grounds of irrelevance or non-application of mind.

options.label: C
options.text: The Supreme Court has held the satisfaction subject to judicial review for mala fides, irrelevance, or non-application of mind.

options.label: D
options.text: Ordinances cannot be challenged in court until they are replaced by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court has held the satisfaction subject to judicial review for mala fides, irrelevance, or non-application of mind..

questions.text: Under the Representation of the People Act and judicial oversight, which statement accurately reflects the Supreme Court's role in election disputes?

options.label: A
options.text: The Election Commission's decisions on election disputes are final and immune from any judicial scrutiny under Article 329.

options.label: B
options.text: The Supreme Court exercises only original jurisdiction under Article 32 in election matters, not appellate jurisdiction.

options.label: C
options.text: The Supreme Court exercises appellate and supervisory jurisdiction under Articles 136 and 32 over Election Commission decisions.

options.label: D
options.text: Election petitions can be filed only in High Courts, and the Supreme Court has no jurisdiction until a High Court decision is appealed.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court exercises appellate and supervisory jurisdiction under Articles 136 and 32 over Election Commission decisions..

questions.text: In the principle of natural justice as applied to quasi-judicial proceedings, which of the following is a settled requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: The rule against bias requires proof of actual bias; mere appearance of bias is insufficient to vitiate a decision.

options.label: B
options.text: A quasi-judicial tribunal's order without reasons does not violate natural justice if the decision is otherwise correct on merits.

options.label: C
options.text: The requirement of a speaking order (reasoned decision) is a settled facet of procedural fairness in quasi-judicial proceedings.

options.label: D
options.text: Post-decisional hearings are never permitted, even in urgent matters like preventive detention under Article 22.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The requirement of a speaking order (reasoned decision) is a settled facet of procedural fairness in quasi-judicial proceedings..

questions.text: Regarding Article 254(2) of the Constitution, what is the effect of the President's assent to a State law that is repugnant to a Union law on a Concurrent List subject?

options.label: A
options.text: The State law becomes immune from any future Parliamentary legislation on that subject.

options.label: B
options.text: The State law prevails in that State, but Parliament retains the power to enact further legislation overriding it.

options.label: C
options.text: The State law prevails only until the Union law is amended or repealed.

options.label: D
options.text: The State law operates only in areas not expressly covered by the Union law.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The State law prevails in that State, but Parliament retains the power to enact further legislation overriding it..

questions.text: Which statement accurately reflects the judicial approach to methods of constitutional interpretation in India?

options.label: A
options.text: Textualism is the sole method used for interpreting Fundamental Rights.

options.label: B
options.text: Purposive and progressive interpretation is prioritized for Fundamental Rights, while textualism may be preferred for procedural provisions.

options.label: C
options.text: The doctrine of Basic Structure applies only to the interpretation of Directive Principles of State Policy.

options.label: D
options.text: Harmonious construction is used exclusively for resolving Centre-State legislative conflicts.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Purposive and progressive interpretation is prioritized for Fundamental Rights, while textualism may be preferred for procedural provisions..

questions.text: With reference to the evolution of locus standi and Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The relaxation of locus standi has completely abolished the requirement of being an 'aggrieved person' in all types of litigation.

options.label: B
options.text: Epistolary jurisdiction allows the Supreme Court to treat letters or newspaper reports as writ petitions, as demonstrated in Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar.

options.label: C
options.text: PILs are now routinely entertained in purely private disputes and service matters without restrictions.

options.label: D
options.text: The judiciary has not imposed any safeguards against frivolous PILs or vexatious litigation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Epistolary jurisdiction allows the Supreme Court to treat letters or newspaper reports as writ petitions, as demonstrated in Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar..

questions.text: What is the primary distinction between the 'doctrine of repugnancy' and the 'doctrine of colourable legislation'?

options.label: A
options.text: Repugnancy deals with conflict between Union and State laws on Concurrent subjects, while colourable legislation questions legislative competence based on the true nature of the law.

options.label: B
options.text: Repugnancy applies only to Union List subjects, while colourable legislation applies to State List subjects.

options.label: C
options.text: Colourable legislation resolves conflicts between two State laws, while repugnancy resolves conflicts between Union and State laws.

options.label: D
options.text: Both doctrines operate exclusively under Article 254 of the Constitution.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Repugnancy deals with conflict between Union and State laws on Concurrent subjects, while colourable legislation questions legislative competence based on the true nature of the law..

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the doctrine of harmonious construction in Centre‑State legislative conflicts?

options.label: A
options.text: It is an interpretive tool used to reconcile Central and State laws on Concurrent subjects before applying the repugnancy clause of Article 254.

options.label: B
options.text: It empowers courts to rewrite legislation so that both Union and State laws can operate simultaneously.

options.label: C
options.text: It automatically gives precedence to Union law over State law on all subjects in the Seventh Schedule.

options.label: D
options.text: It applies only when the conflict arises between laws on the Union List.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It is an interpretive tool used to reconcile Central and State laws on Concurrent subjects before applying the repugnancy clause of Article 254..

questions.text: According to the Supreme Court Bar Association v. Union of India (1998) guidelines, which procedural safeguard is mandatory for the appointment of an amicus curiae?

options.label: A
options.text: Reasons for appointment must be recorded, the amicus’s qualifications disclosed, and the parties notified.

options.label: B
options.text: The amicus may introduce new factual evidence to supplement the record.

options.label: C
options.text: The amicus represents the party that is inadequately represented in the proceedings.

options.label: D
options.text: Appointment of an amicus is compulsory in every constitutional matter before the Court.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Reasons for appointment must be recorded, the amicus’s qualifications disclosed, and the parties notified..

questions.text: Regarding the protection of tenure for elected representatives under the 73rd Amendment, which of the following statements is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: A Panchayat can be dissolved by the State Government at any time on grounds of administrative inefficiency.

options.label: B
options.text: The Governor can dissolve a Panchayat before the expiry of its term only on grounds specified in the Constitution.

options.label: C
options.text: The State Election Commission has the authority to dissolve a Panchayat if elections are not held on time.

options.label: D
options.text: A Panchayat dissolved before its term expires must be reconstituted within three months, failing which the State Government assumes its functions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Governor can dissolve a Panchayat before the expiry of its term only on grounds specified in the Constitution..

questions.text: The 74th Amendment mandates the constitution of Ward Committees in municipalities. What is the population threshold specified in the Constitution for this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: One lakh or more

options.label: B
options.text: Two lakh or more

options.label: C
options.text: Three lakh or more

options.label: D
options.text: Five lakh or more

questions.solution: Correct answer: Three lakh or more.

questions.text: With reference to the State Finance Commission (SFC) mandated by the 73rd and 74th Amendments, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The SFC is constituted by the President of India every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats and Municipalities.

options.label: B
options.text: The SFC recommends the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the State and local bodies, and determines the grants-in-aid to local bodies from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

options.label: C
options.text: The SFC's recommendations are binding on the State Government and do not require legislative approval.

options.label: D
options.text: The SFC replaces the Central Finance Commission in matters relating to local body finances.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The SFC recommends the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the State and local bodies, and determines the grants-in-aid to local bodies from the Consolidated Fund of the State..

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the constitution of a Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC)?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 243ZD

options.label: B
options.text: Article 243ZE

options.label: C
options.text: Article 243ZB

options.label: D
options.text: Article 243ZC

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 243ZE.

questions.text: What is the share of local bodies in the divisible pool of taxes as recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission?

options.label: A
options.text: 4.31% of GDP

options.label: B
options.text: 4.31% of the divisible pool of taxes

options.label: C
options.text: 3.5% of the divisible pool of taxes

options.label: D
options.text: 5% of the net proceeds of shareable taxes

questions.solution: Correct answer: 4.31% of the divisible pool of taxes.

questions.text: What is the constitutional and legal status of parastatal agencies such as Development Authorities and Smart City SPVs?

options.label: A
options.text: They are constitutionally mandated bodies under Article 243ZE.

options.label: B
options.text: They are created by state statutes and lack direct electoral accountability.

options.label: C
options.text: They are established by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act.

options.label: D
options.text: They derive their statutory authority from the District Planning Committee.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They are created by state statutes and lack direct electoral accountability..

questions.text: In which category of municipalities is the constitution of Ward Committees mandatory under the Constitution?

options.label: A
options.text: All municipalities irrespective of population size.

options.label: B
options.text: Municipalities with a population of one lakh or more.

options.label: C
options.text: Municipalities with a population of three lakh or more.

options.label: D
options.text: Only in Municipal Corporations.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Municipalities with a population of three lakh or more..

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution mandates the establishment of a State Election Commission for the conduct of elections to Panchayats?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 243K

options.label: B
options.text: Article 243ZA

options.label: C
options.text: Article 243A

options.label: D
options.text: Article 243B

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 243K.

questions.text: The E‑Panchayat initiative is a digital transformation project for Panchayati Raj Institutions. Under which framework is it implemented?

options.label: A
options.text: As a State‑level scheme funded by the State government

options.label: B
options.text: As a Centrally Sponsored Mission Mode Project under the National e‑Governance Plan (NeGP)

options.label: C
options.text: As a private‑public partnership managed by NIC

options.label: D
options.text: Exclusively under the Ministry of Rural Development without NeGP linkage

questions.solution: Correct answer: As a Centrally Sponsored Mission Mode Project under the National e‑Governance Plan (NeGP).

questions.text: Social audit under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) is distinct from statutory audit. Which feature best characterises social audit?

options.label: A
options.text: Conducted by professional chartered accountants appointed by the State

options.label: B
options.text: A community‑led process with a statutory basis under MGNREGA

options.label: C
options.text: Optional for Gram Panchayats and conducted only on demand

options.label: D
options.text: Performed by the State Audit Department as part of regular financial audit

questions.solution: Correct answer: A community‑led process with a statutory basis under MGNREGA.

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the powers of the Gram Sabha under the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) from the Gram Sabha in non-Scheduled Areas?

options.label: A
options.text: Under PESA, the Gram Sabha has only advisory powers over minor forest produce, while in non-Scheduled Areas it has ownership rights.

options.label: B
options.text: Under PESA, the Gram Sabha enjoys substantive legislative-type powers over minor forest produce and land acquisition, unlike the advisory role in non-Scheduled Areas.

options.label: C
options.text: The Gram Sabha under PESA requires State Government approval for all resolutions, whereas in non-Scheduled Areas it functions autonomously.

options.label: D
options.text: PESA grants the Gram Sabha judicial powers to adjudicate criminal cases, a power absent in non-Scheduled Areas.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Under PESA, the Gram Sabha enjoys substantive legislative-type powers over minor forest produce and land acquisition, unlike the advisory role in non-Scheduled Areas..

questions.text: Regarding the Model Municipal Law (MML) 2003, which of the following statements is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a binding Central statute that all States must adopt without modification under Article 243Q of the Constitution.

options.label: B
options.text: It provides for a directly elected Mayor with a five-year term and executive powers, but State adaptations vary widely in mayoral powers and ward committee effectiveness.

options.label: C
options.text: It mandates the constitution of Ward Committees only in municipalities with a population exceeding 10 lakhs.

options.label: D
options.text: It abolishes the post of Municipal Commissioner and transfers all executive authority to the Mayor.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It provides for a directly elected Mayor with a five-year term and executive powers, but State adaptations vary widely in mayoral powers and ward committee effectiveness..

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly identifies a specific recommendation of the L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) regarding Panchayati Raj Institutions?

options.label: A
options.text: It recommended a two-tier system of Panchayati Raj with Zilla Parishad at the district level.

options.label: B
options.text: It recommended direct elections for all three tiers of Panchayati Raj Institutions.

options.label: C
options.text: It suggested the establishment of Nyaya Panchayats for speedy justice at the local level.

options.label: D
options.text: It described PRIs as "grass without roots" and recommended the Zilla Parishad as the principal body for development programmes.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It suggested the establishment of Nyaya Panchayats for speedy justice at the local level..

questions.text: With reference to the composition of District Planning Committees (DPCs) as mandated by the Constitution, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: All members of the DPC are nominated by the State Government.

options.label: B
options.text: Four-fifths of the members are elected by the elected members of the Panchayats and Municipalities in the district from amongst themselves.

options.label: C
options.text: The Chairperson of the DPC is mandatorily the District Collector in all states.

options.label: D
options.text: DPCs are constituted under Article 243ZE of the Constitution.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Four-fifths of the members are elected by the elected members of the Panchayats and Municipalities in the district from amongst themselves..

questions.text: In the context of fiscal autonomy of local bodies in India, which one of the following sources of funds is classified as 'untied funds' allowing discretion in expenditure?

options.label: A
options.text: Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS)

options.label: B
options.text: Finance Commission Grants

options.label: C
options.text: Funds released under specific State Government Schemes with strict guidelines

options.label: D
options.text: Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) funds

questions.solution: Correct answer: Finance Commission Grants.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the legal basis and governance structure of Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) in urban development?

options.label: A
options.text: SPVs are statutory bodies constituted directly under Article 243Q of the Constitution.

options.label: B
options.text: SPVs are typically registered under the Companies Act, 2013, and their boards are usually chaired by senior bureaucrats.

options.label: C
options.text: The Mayor of the Municipal Corporation holds executive control over the SPV board as its Chairperson.

options.label: D
options.text: SPVs derive their legal mandate from the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act.

questions.solution: Correct answer: SPVs are typically registered under the Companies Act, 2013, and their boards are usually chaired by senior bureaucrats..

questions.text: Regarding the mandate and process of Social Audit in India, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment explicitly mandates social audits for all rural development schemes.

options.label: B
options.text: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005, explicitly mandates social audits of its works.

options.label: C
options.text: The Gram Sabha plays only an advisory role in the social audit process under MGNREGA.

options.label: D
options.text: Social Audit units function under the direct administrative control of the District Collector.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005, explicitly mandates social audits of its works..

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the horizontal fiscal equalisation formula typically adopted by State Finance Commissions for Panchayats and Municipalities?

options.label: A
options.text: Population is assigned the lowest weight (10-15%) while geographical area receives the highest weight (50-60%).

options.label: B
options.text: The formula weights population (50-60%), geographical area (10-15%), a deprivation index (20-30%), and revenue effort (5-10%).

options.label: C
options.text: Revenue effort is given the highest weight (40-50%) to incentivise own-source revenue mobilisation, while population receives only 10-15%.

options.label: D
options.text: Deprivation index based on SC/ST population and literacy is excluded from the formula, which relies solely on population and area.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The formula weights population (50-60%), geographical area (10-15%), a deprivation index (20-30%), and revenue effort (5-10%)..

questions.text: Regarding reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in Panchayats and Municipalities, which statement is constitutionally accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Articles 243-D and 243-T mandate a fixed 27% reservation for OBCs in all States, similar to SC/ST reservation.

options.label: B
options.text: The Constitution requires States to provide OBC reservation up to 50% of total seats, subject to the triple test laid down by the Supreme Court.

options.label: C
options.text: Articles 243-D(6) and 243-T(6) empower State Legislatures to make provision for OBC reservation by law, but do not prescribe a constitutional quota.

options.label: D
options.text: OBC reservation in local bodies is a Union subject under Article 246, and Parliament has enacted a uniform law for all States.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Articles 243-D(6) and 243-T(6) empower State Legislatures to make provision for OBC reservation by law, but do not prescribe a constitutional quota..

questions.text: The Supreme Court's judicial interpretation of Articles 243-G (Panchayats) and 243-W (Municipalities) has established which of the following principles regarding functional devolution?

options.label: A
options.text: These Articles are merely enabling provisions; State Legislatures have complete discretion whether to devolve any functions to local bodies.

options.label: B
options.text: The Articles impose a positive legislative duty on States to devolve functions, and the absence of activity mapping renders the constitutional mandate unfulfilled.

options.label: C
options.text: Functional devolution under these Articles is limited to the 29 subjects in the Eleventh Schedule and 18 subjects in the Twelfth Schedule, with no scope for additional functions.

options.label: D
options.text: The Courts have held that financial devolution is a prerequisite for functional devolution, making Article 243-H/243-X justiciable before Articles 243-G/243-W.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Articles impose a positive legislative duty on States to devolve functions, and the absence of activity mapping renders the constitutional mandate unfulfilled..

questions.text: With reference to the impact of Goods and Services Tax (GST) on Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The GST compensation cess is directly devolved to ULBs by the Union Government as a replacement for octroi and entry tax.

options.label: B
options.text: ULBs lost significant own-source revenue from taxes subsumed under GST (octroi, entry tax, advertisement tax), and GST compensation cess flows to States, not directly to ULBs.

options.label: C
options.text: Property tax and municipal bonds were subsumed under GST, forcing ULBs to rely entirely on State grants for revenue.

options.label: D
options.text: The Fifteenth Finance Commission has recommended that 50% of the GST compensation cess be earmarked exclusively for ULBs as untied grants.

questions.solution: Correct answer: ULBs lost significant own-source revenue from taxes subsumed under GST (octroi, entry tax, advertisement tax), and GST compensation cess flows to States, not directly to ULBs..

questions.text: The integration of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) with District Planning Committees (DPCs) as a convergence mechanism requires which of the following operational links?

options.label: A
options.text: GPDP data integration into DPC planning software, resource pooling of CSS funds tagged to GPDP activities, and quarterly monitoring with corrective directives by the DPC.

options.label: B
options.text: Mandatory merger of all Panchayat bank accounts into a single district-level fund controlled by the DPC, with the District Collector as the sole signatory.

options.label: C
options.text: Annual submission of GPDPs to the State Finance Commission, which then reallocates funds based on a uniform per-capita formula across all districts.

options.label: D
options.text: The DPC functions solely as a consultative forum; final approval of consolidated district plans rests with the State Planning Board.

questions.solution: Correct answer: GPDP data integration into DPC planning software, resource pooling of CSS funds tagged to GPDP activities, and quarterly monitoring with corrective directives by the DPC..

questions.text: Which State's Panchayat Raj Act transferred all 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule along with matching functionaries and finances, and established a robust District Planning Committee?

options.label: A
options.text: Kerala

options.label: B
options.text: Maharashtra

options.label: C
options.text: Karnataka

options.label: D
options.text: Tamil Nadu

questions.solution: Correct answer: Kerala.

questions.text: Under the Model Concession Agreement (MCA) 2017 for municipal PPPs, which category of risk is retained by the Urban Local Body (ULB)?

options.label: A
options.text: Construction risk

options.label: B
options.text: Demand risk

options.label: C
options.text: Regulatory risk

options.label: D
options.text: Technology risk

questions.solution: Correct answer: Regulatory risk.

questions.text: What is a prerequisite for integrating District Disaster Management Plans (DDMPs) with Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) and Municipal plans?

options.label: A
options.text: Automatic integration under the Disaster Management Act

options.label: B
options.text: A deliberate joint‑planning mechanism

options.label: C
options.text: Central monitoring by the Ministry of Home Affairs

options.label: D
options.text: Uniform State legislation on disaster management

questions.solution: Correct answer: A deliberate joint‑planning mechanism.

questions.text: According to the Model Municipal Law, 2003, what composition and tenure does it propose for the State Election Commission (SEC)?

options.label: A
options.text: Single‑member SEC with a five‑year term

options.label: B
options.text: Three‑member SEC with a fixed term

options.label: C
options.text: SEC appointed by the Governor for six years

options.label: D
options.text: SEC with the same tenure and removal process as the Election Commission of India

questions.solution: Correct answer: Three‑member SEC with a fixed term.

questions.text: Which indicator is included in the Fifteenth Finance Commission's performance‑based grant for Panchayats to promote gender‑responsive budgeting?

options.label: A
options.text: Presence of a Women's Component Plan

options.label: B
options.text: Earmarking of at least 10 % of plan outlay for women

options.label: C
options.text: Gender‑disaggregated data reporting for all Centrally Sponsored Schemes

options.label: D
options.text: Establishment of a Gender Budget Cell in the Panchayat

questions.solution: Correct answer: Gender‑disaggregated data reporting for all Centrally Sponsored Schemes.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly states the procedural requirement for moving an Adjournment Motion in the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: Support of at least 30 members and the Speaker's consent

options.label: B
options.text: Support of at least 50 members and the Speaker's consent

options.label: C
options.text: Support of at least 50 members only

options.label: D
options.text: Support of at least 100 members and the Speaker's consent

questions.solution: Correct answer: Support of at least 50 members and the Speaker's consent.

questions.text: Regarding the Speaker's certification of a Money Bill under Article 110, which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The certification is final and cannot be challenged in any court

options.label: B
options.text: The certification can be challenged only through a parliamentary resolution

options.label: C
options.text: The certification is subject to judicial review and cannot be a colourable exercise of power

options.label: D
options.text: The certification requires prior concurrence of the Rajya Sabha

questions.solution: Correct answer: The certification is subject to judicial review and cannot be a colourable exercise of power.

questions.text: What is the correct status of Department‑Related Standing Committee (DRSC) reports in relation to the executive?

options.label: A
options.text: They are binding on the government and must be implemented

options.label: B
options.text: They are recommendatory, but the government must present an Action Taken Report

options.label: C
options.text: They are advisory only to the Speaker and have no executive relevance

options.label: D
options.text: They automatically become law once adopted by the House

questions.solution: Correct answer: They are recommendatory, but the government must present an Action Taken Report.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Policy Cut Motion from a Token Cut Motion?

options.label: A
options.text: Policy Cut reduces the demand to Re 1; Token Cut reduces the demand by Rs 100

options.label: B
options.text: Policy Cut reduces the demand by Rs 100; Token Cut reduces the demand to Re 1

options.label: C
options.text: Both reduce the demand to Re 1

options.label: D
options.text: Both reduce the demand by Rs 100

questions.solution: Correct answer: Policy Cut reduces the demand to Re 1; Token Cut reduces the demand by Rs 100.

questions.text: Which statement accurately describes the Rajya Sabha's powers in financial legislation?

options.label: A
options.text: It can amend or reject the Appropriation Bill

options.label: B
options.text: It can introduce Money Bills under Article 110

options.label: C
options.text: It can only discuss and make recommendations on the Finance Bill and cannot vote on Demands for Grants

options.label: D
options.text: It possesses a veto over the Appropriation Bill

questions.solution: Correct answer: It can only discuss and make recommendations on the Finance Bill and cannot vote on Demands for Grants.

questions.text: What are the prescribed notice periods for a Starred Question and a Short‑Notice Question in the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: 15 clear days for Starred; 3 days for Short‑Notice

options.label: B
options.text: 10 clear days for Starred; 5 days for Short‑Notice

options.label: C
options.text: 20 clear days for Starred; 7 days for Short‑Notice

options.label: D
options.text: 15 clear days for both Starred and Short‑Notice

questions.solution: Correct answer: 15 clear days for Starred; 3 days for Short‑Notice.

questions.text: How much maximum debate time is allotted to each Private Member's Bill in the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: Thirty minutes on Fridays (or the last sitting day of the week)

options.label: B
options.text: One hour on any sitting day

options.label: C
options.text: Two hours on Fridays

options.label: D
options.text: No fixed limit; the Speaker decides case by case

questions.solution: Correct answer: Thirty minutes on Fridays (or the last sitting day of the week).

questions.text: What is the nature of the recommendations made by the Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) and what follow‑up is required from the government?

options.label: A
options.text: Binding on the government; no further report needed

options.label: B
options.text: Advisory, but the government must submit an Action Taken Report

options.label: C
options.text: Purely advisory with no obligation for an Action Taken Report

options.label: D
options.text: Enforceable by Parliament through a separate resolution

questions.solution: Correct answer: Advisory, but the government must submit an Action Taken Report.

questions.text: Which category of international treaties must be enacted by Parliament before they become domestically enforceable?

options.label: A
options.text: All treaties signed by the executive

options.label: B
options.text: Only treaties that require domestic legislation for implementation

options.label: C
options.text: Only executive agreements

options.label: D
options.text: Only treaties ratified by the President

questions.solution: Correct answer: Only treaties that require domestic legislation for implementation.

questions.text: In which House can a Motion of No‑Confidence be moved, and what is the minimum number of members whose written support is required?

options.label: A
options.text: Lok Sabha; at least fifty members

options.label: B
options.text: Rajya Sabha; at least fifty members

options.label: C
options.text: Lok Sabha; at least one hundred members

options.label: D
options.text: Either House; at least fifty members

questions.solution: Correct answer: Lok Sabha; at least fifty members.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the chairmanship of the Ethics Committee and the Committee on Privileges in the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: Both committees are chaired by the Speaker.

options.label: B
options.text: The Ethics Committee is chaired by the Deputy Speaker, while the Privileges Committee elects its own chairperson.

options.label: C
options.text: The Ethics Committee elects its own chairperson, while the Privileges Committee is chaired by the Deputy Speaker by convention.

options.label: D
options.text: The chairpersons of both committees are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Ethics Committee elects its own chairperson, while the Privileges Committee is chaired by the Deputy Speaker by convention..

questions.text: What is the primary limitation of the Committee on Government Assurances in ensuring executive accountability?

options.label: A
options.text: It can impose penalties on ministers who fail to fulfil assurances.

options.label: B
options.text: It has the power to initiate judicial proceedings against defaulting ministries.

options.label: C
options.text: It only reports on the implementation of assurances and relies on political pressure for compliance.

options.label: D
options.text: It can amend the Rules of Procedure to make assurances legally binding.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It only reports on the implementation of assurances and relies on political pressure for compliance..

questions.text: Which statement is true regarding the constitutional scope of an ordinance promulgated by the President?

options.label: A
options.text: An ordinance can amend the Constitution if ratified by a simple majority in Parliament.

options.label: B
options.text: An ordinance cannot amend the Constitution; constitutional amendments require the Article 368 procedure.

options.label: C
options.text: An ordinance can override a Supreme Court judgment on a constitutional matter.

options.label: D
options.text: An ordinance remains in force indefinitely unless disapproved by both Houses.

questions.solution: Correct answer: An ordinance cannot amend the Constitution; constitutional amendments require the Article 368 procedure..

questions.text: How does a Calling Attention Motion differ from a Short Duration Discussion in terms of ministerial response?

options.label: A
options.text: Both require a formal motion and a mandatory ministerial reply.

options.label: B
options.text: A Calling Attention Motion mandates a ministerial reply, whereas a Short Duration Discussion involves a ministerial reply but no formal motion.

options.label: C
options.text: A Short Duration Discussion requires a ministerial reply, while a Calling Attention Motion does not.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither device obliges the minister to reply; both are purely deliberative.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A Calling Attention Motion mandates a ministerial reply, whereas a Short Duration Discussion involves a ministerial reply but no formal motion..

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) of Parliament is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Its recommendations are legally binding on the House.

options.label: B
options.text: It is chaired by the Leader of the Opposition.

options.label: C
options.text: It allocates time for government bills, private members' bills, and discussions, and its recommendations are usually followed by the presiding officer.

options.label: D
options.text: It decides on the passage of constitutional amendment bills.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It allocates time for government bills, private members' bills, and discussions, and its recommendations are usually followed by the presiding officer..

questions.text: Which of the following is true about the constitutional amendment procedure under Article 368?

options.label: A
options.text: A constitutional amendment bill requires a simple majority in each House.

options.label: B
options.text: The President may withhold assent to a constitutional amendment bill.

options.label: C
options.text: State ratification is required for all constitutional amendments.

options.label: D
options.text: An amendment affecting federal provisions listed in Article 368(2) requires ratification by at least half of the state legislatures, and the President's assent is obligatory.

questions.solution: Correct answer: An amendment affecting federal provisions listed in Article 368(2) requires ratification by at least half of the state legislatures, and the President's assent is obligatory..

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes India's engagement with the Inter‑Parliamentary Union (IPU) and the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA)?

options.label: A
options.text: The IPU is a Commonwealth‑specific association while the CPA is a global inter‑parliamentary organisation.

options.label: B
options.text: The Indian Parliamentary Group serves as the national group for both the IPU and the CPA.

options.label: C
options.text: Resolutions adopted at the IPU automatically become part of Indian domestic law.

options.label: D
options.text: India has never hosted an IPU Assembly.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Indian Parliamentary Group serves as the national group for both the IPU and the CPA..

questions.text: Regarding the Speaker's decisions in the Lok Sabha, which one of the following is subject to judicial review?

options.label: A
options.text: Certification of a Bill as a Money Bill under Article 110.

options.label: B
options.text: Rulings on points of order raised during Question Hour.

options.label: C
options.text: Decisions on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law).

options.label: D
options.text: Allocation of time for discussion by the Business Advisory Committee.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Decisions on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law)..

questions.text: What is the primary nature of recommendations made by Department-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) to the Executive?

options.label: A
options.text: Binding on the Ministry concerned, requiring mandatory implementation.

options.label: B
options.text: Advisory in nature, which the Executive may accept or reject.

options.label: C
options.text: Legally enforceable through a writ of mandamus by the High Courts.

options.label: D
options.text: Automatically incorporated into the final legislation without Parliamentary vote.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Advisory in nature, which the Executive may accept or reject..

questions.text: The 'Guillotine' is a parliamentary procedural device used for which specific purpose?

options.label: A
options.text: To censure the Council of Ministers for a specific policy failure.

options.label: B
options.text: To put outstanding Demands for Grants to vote without discussion due to time constraints.

options.label: C
options.text: To terminate a No-Confidence Motion before it is put to vote.

options.label: D
options.text: To suspend a member for grossly disorderly conduct in the House.

questions.solution: Correct answer: To put outstanding Demands for Grants to vote without discussion due to time constraints..

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the five indicia identified by the Supreme Court in Pradyut Bordoloi v. Swapan Roy (2001) for determining an "office of profit"?

options.label: A
options.text: Government appointment

options.label: B
options.text: Government power to remove

options.label: C
options.text: Government remuneration

options.label: D
options.text: Government ownership of the office premises

questions.solution: Correct answer: Government ownership of the office premises.

questions.text: Under the parliamentary control mechanisms for delegated legislation, which procedure requires a resolution of the House to annul a rule or regulation?

options.label: A
options.text: Laying requirement

options.label: B
options.text: Negative resolution

options.label: C
options.text: Committee on Subordinate Legislation recommendation

options.label: D
options.text: Judicial review

questions.solution: Correct answer: Negative resolution.

questions.text: Which statement accurately reflects the parliamentary scrutiny of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) reports?

options.label: A
options.text: All CAG reports are automatically debated in Parliament

options.label: B
options.text: The Public Accounts Committee selects only a fraction of CAG reports for examination

options.label: C
options.text: The CAG's expenditure is voted through the Demand for Grants process

options.label: D
options.text: The Election Commission's reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Public Accounts Committee selects only a fraction of CAG reports for examination.

questions.text: In Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that the Speaker's decision on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is:

options.label: A
options.text: Final and not subject to judicial review

options.label: B
options.text: Subject to judicial review for mala fides, perversity, or violation of natural justice

options.label: C
options.text: Only reviewable by the High Court

options.label: D
options.text: Binding on the Election Commission

questions.solution: Correct answer: Subject to judicial review for mala fides, perversity, or violation of natural justice.

questions.text: What is the parliamentary approval requirement for a Proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 of the Constitution?

options.label: A
options.text: Simple majority in both Houses

options.label: B
options.text: Special majority in both Houses

options.label: C
options.text: Simple majority in Lok Sabha only

options.label: D
options.text: Special majority in Lok Sabha and simple majority in Rajya Sabha

questions.solution: Correct answer: Special majority in both Houses.

questions.text: Regarding the appointment and tenure of the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Appointed by the Prime Minister on the recommendation of the Speaker for a fixed term of five years.

options.label: B
options.text: Appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Speaker and holds office until the age of 60 years or resignation, whichever is earlier.

options.label: C
options.text: Appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

options.label: D
options.text: Appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and holds office until the dissolution of the House.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Speaker and holds office until the age of 60 years or resignation, whichever is earlier..

questions.text: In the context of negative resolution procedure for delegated legislation, what is the consequence if Parliament takes no action within the stipulated period?

options.label: A
options.text: The delegated legislation lapses and ceases to have effect.

options.label: B
options.text: The delegated legislation is deemed to have been approved and continues in force.

options.label: C
options.text: The matter is automatically referred to the Committee on Subordinate Legislation for detailed scrutiny.

options.label: D
options.text: The government is required to re-promulgate the legislation with modifications.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The delegated legislation is deemed to have been approved and continues in force..

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution provides for free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 21

options.label: B
options.text: Article 21A

options.label: C
options.text: Article 45

options.label: D
options.text: Article 46

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 21A.

questions.text: MGNREGA guarantees how many days of wage employment per rural household per year?

options.label: A
options.text: 50 days

options.label: B
options.text: 75 days

options.label: C
options.text: 100 days

options.label: D
options.text: 150 days

questions.solution: Correct answer: 100 days.

questions.text: Which of the following is a Directive Principle (non-justiciable), not a Fundamental Right?

options.label: A
options.text: Abolition of untouchability

options.label: B
options.text: Right to education (6–14 years)

options.label: C
options.text: Promotion of educational interests of SCs and STs

options.label: D
options.text: Prohibition of child labour

questions.solution: Correct answer: Promotion of educational interests of SCs and STs.

questions.text: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to what percentage of the rural population under TPDS?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 75%.

questions.text: Which Supreme Court judgement recognised the right of transgender persons to self-identify their gender?

options.label: A
options.text: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018)

options.label: B
options.text: NALSA v. Union of India (2014)

options.label: C
options.text: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)

options.label: D
options.text: Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017)

questions.solution: Correct answer: NALSA v. Union of India (2014).

questions.text: Ayushman Bharat PMJAY provides health insurance cover of how much per family per year?

options.label: A
options.text: ₹1 lakh

options.label: B
options.text: ₹3 lakh

options.label: C
options.text: ₹5 lakh

options.label: D
options.text: ₹10 lakh

questions.solution: Correct answer: ₹5 lakh.

questions.text: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 gave constitutional status to which body?

options.label: A
options.text: National Commission for Scheduled Castes

options.label: B
options.text: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes

options.label: C
options.text: National Commission for Backward Classes

options.label: D
options.text: National Commission for Women

questions.solution: Correct answer: National Commission for Backward Classes.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a component of the National Health Mission (NHM)?

options.label: A
options.text: National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)

options.label: B
options.text: National Urban Health Mission (NUHM)

options.label: C
options.text: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY)

options.label: D
options.text: Flexipool for NCDs and Health Systems

questions.solution: Correct answer: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY).

questions.text: Under Article 74 of the Constitution, what is the extent of the President's discretion regarding the advice of the Council of Ministers?

options.label: A
options.text: The President may reject the advice outright and act independently.

options.label: B
options.text: The President must act on the advice but may require the Council to reconsider it once.

options.label: C
options.text: The President can act independently in all matters except financial bills.

options.label: D
options.text: The advice of the Council of Ministers is not binding on the President.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The President must act on the advice but may require the Council to reconsider it once..

questions.text: How is the Vice‑President of India elected?

options.label: A
options.text: Directly by the people of India.

options.label: B
options.text: By an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament.

options.label: C
options.text: By the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

options.label: D
options.text: By the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies.

questions.solution: Correct answer: By an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament..

questions.text: What change did the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) make regarding the President's ordinance‑making power?

options.label: A
options.text: Extended the maximum life of an ordinance to six months.

options.label: B
options.text: Provided that an ordinance cannot be promulgated when both Houses of Parliament are in session.

options.label: C
options.text: Removed the President's power to promulgate ordinances altogether.

options.label: D
options.text: Allowed the President to issue ordinances without the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Provided that an ordinance cannot be promulgated when both Houses of Parliament are in session..

questions.text: The 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) placed a ceiling on the size of the Union Council of Ministers. What is that ceiling?

options.label: A
options.text: 10 % of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

options.label: B
options.text: 15 % of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

options.label: C
options.text: 20 % of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

options.label: D
options.text: No ceiling; the size is determined by the Prime Minister.

questions.solution: Correct answer: 15 % of the total strength of the Lok Sabha..

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the creation of All‑India Services, and which body recruits them?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 309 – Staff Selection Commission.

options.label: B
options.text: Article 312 – Union Public Service Commission.

options.label: C
options.text: Article 315 – State Public Service Commissions.

options.label: D
options.text: Article 320 – Department of Personnel and Training.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 312 – Union Public Service Commission..

questions.text: Regarding the ordinance-making power of the President under Article 123, which principle was laid down by the Supreme Court in D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1987)?

options.label: A
options.text: The President's satisfaction regarding the necessity of immediate legislation is entirely subjective and non-justiciable.

options.label: B
options.text: An ordinance can be repromulgated indefinitely without legislative approval as long as the President deems it necessary.

options.label: C
options.text: Repeated repromulgation of ordinances without legislative approval constitutes a fraud on the Constitution and an abuse of the ordinance-making power.

options.label: D
options.text: Ordinances lapse automatically after six weeks of Parliament's reassembly only if both Houses pass a resolution disapproving them.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Repeated repromulgation of ordinances without legislative approval constitutes a fraud on the Constitution and an abuse of the ordinance-making power..

questions.text: Which of the following statements about Cabinet Committees in India is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Cabinet Committees are statutory bodies established under an Act of Parliament.

options.label: B
options.text: The Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) includes the National Security Adviser (NSA) as a permanent invitee.

options.label: C
options.text: The Cabinet Secretariat has no role in the functioning of Cabinet Committees.

options.label: D
options.text: Ad-hoc Groups of Ministers (GoMs) submit their recommendations directly to the Prime Minister, bypassing standing Cabinet Committees.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) includes the National Security Adviser (NSA) as a permanent invitee..

questions.text: In T.S.R. Subramanian v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court issued directions to insulate civil services from political interference. Which of the following was NOT a direction given by the Court?

options.label: A
options.text: Establishment of a Civil Services Board at the Centre and in each state to recommend transfers, postings, and disciplinary actions.

options.label: B
options.text: Mandating fixed tenures for key posts such as Director General of Police and Chief Secretary.

options.label: C
options.text: Requiring that any premature transfer be recorded with reasons.

options.label: D
options.text: Making the Civil Services Board's recommendations binding on the political executive with no discretion to deviate.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Making the Civil Services Board's recommendations binding on the political executive with no discretion to deviate..

questions.text: Regarding Article 143 of the Constitution, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The Supreme Court's advisory opinion is binding on the President and the Council of Ministers.

options.label: B
options.text: The President may refer only questions of fact, not questions of law, to the Supreme Court.

options.label: C
options.text: The advisory opinion is not binding but carries significant persuasive authority.

options.label: D
options.text: The Supreme Court is constitutionally compelled to answer every reference made by the President.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The advisory opinion is not binding but carries significant persuasive authority..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) from the Cabinet Secretariat?

options.label: A
options.text: Both are constitutional bodies established under Article 74 of the Constitution.

options.label: B
options.text: The PMO is a constitutional‑administrative body, while the Cabinet Secretariat is a political office.

options.label: C
options.text: The PMO is a political office, whereas the Cabinet Secretariat is a constitutional‑administrative body.

options.label: D
options.text: The two offices are functionally interchangeable and share identical accountability mechanisms.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The PMO is a political office, whereas the Cabinet Secretariat is a constitutional‑administrative body..

questions.text: Under the doctrine of pleasure (Article 310) and the safeguards of Article 311, which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 311 protections apply to all civil servants from the date of recruitment, including probationers.

options.label: B
options.text: Article 311 protections apply only after a servant has been appointed to a substantive post, not during probation.

options.label: C
options.text: Parliament cannot modify the procedural safeguards of Article 311 through ordinary legislation.

options.label: D
options.text: The protections of Article 311 extend to employees of public sector undertakings and autonomous bodies.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 311 protections apply only after a servant has been appointed to a substantive post, not during probation..

questions.text: What change did the Cadre Allocation Policy, 2017 introduce for All India Services officers?

options.label: A
options.text: It abolished the state‑cadre system and created a single national cadre pool.

options.label: B
options.text: It introduced a zone‑based allocation requiring officers to serve in at least one cadre outside their home zone.

options.label: C
options.text: It allowed officers to choose any state cadre solely on the basis of personal preference.

options.label: D
options.text: It removed the mandatory central deputation requirement for all AIS officers.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It introduced a zone‑based allocation requiring officers to serve in at least one cadre outside their home zone..

questions.text: With reference to the imposition of President's Rule under Article 356, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The President's satisfaction is absolute and not subject to judicial review.

options.label: B
options.text: The proclamation must be approved by Parliament within one month.

options.label: C
options.text: The Supreme Court in S.R. Bommai mandated a floor test in the State Assembly within a reasonable time, preferably 48 hours, before imposition.

options.label: D
options.text: The dissolution of the State Assembly is a mandatory and routine sequel to the proclamation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court in S.R. Bommai mandated a floor test in the State Assembly within a reasonable time, preferably 48 hours, before imposition..

questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding the President's pardoning power under Article 72: 1. It is an absolute discretionary power of the President. 2. It is exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers. 3. It is immune from judicial review. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 only

options.label: C
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: D
options.text: 1, 2 and 3

questions.solution: Correct answer: 2 only.

questions.text: In the context of a minority government or a hung Parliament, which of the following accurately describes the President's discretion regarding the dissolution of the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: The President is bound to dissolve the Lok Sabha immediately on the advice of the Prime Minister.

options.label: B
options.text: The President may refuse dissolution if a viable alternative government can be formed.

options.label: C
options.text: The President must refer the matter to the Supreme Court for advisory opinion before dissolving the House.

options.label: D
options.text: The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha only after a confidence motion is defeated on the floor of the House.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The President may refuse dissolution if a viable alternative government can be formed..

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the 360-degree Performance Appraisal Report (PAR) under Mission Karmayogi is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It applies to all civil servants from the level of Assistant Section Officer upwards.

options.label: B
options.text: It replaces the Annual Confidential Report (ACR) system for all Group A and Group B officers.

options.label: C
options.text: It applies only from the Under Secretary level upward, while lower-level officers continue under the older ACR system.

options.label: D
options.text: It is administered solely by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) without any role for the Capacity Building Commission.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It applies only from the Under Secretary level upward, while lower-level officers continue under the older ACR system..

questions.text: With reference to Financial Emergency under Article 360 of the Constitution, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It has been proclaimed once in 1991 during the balance of payments crisis.

options.label: B
options.text: During its operation, the President may direct the reduction of salaries of all persons serving in the State, including judges of the High Courts.

options.label: C
options.text: The proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month.

options.label: D
options.text: The provision has never been invoked since the commencement of the Constitution.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The provision has never been invoked since the commencement of the Constitution..

questions.text: In B.P. Singhal v. Union of India (2010), the Supreme Court held that the President's pleasure doctrine under Article 156 for removal of a Governor:

options.label: A
options.text: Is absolute and not subject to judicial review on any ground

options.label: B
options.text: Is not absolute; removal must not be arbitrary, mala fide or based on extraneous considerations

options.label: C
options.text: Requires prior consultation with the Chief Minister of the concerned state

options.label: D
options.text: Requires a resolution passed by the State Legislative Assembly

questions.solution: Correct answer: Is not absolute; removal must not be arbitrary, mala fide or based on extraneous considerations.

questions.text: The Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) derives its authority from:

options.label: A
options.text: A specific parliamentary statute enacted under Article 77

options.label: B
options.text: The executive's prerogative and the Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules

options.label: C
options.text: A constitutional provision under Article 74(2)

options.label: D
options.text: A resolution of the Union Cabinet passed in 1947

questions.solution: Correct answer: The executive's prerogative and the Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules.

questions.text: Regarding the Union Public Service Commission's role in disciplinary matters against civil servants, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The UPSC's advice is binding on the President

options.label: B
options.text: The UPSC's advice is advisory, but non-consultation can invalidate the disciplinary order

options.label: C
options.text: The UPSC has no role in disciplinary matters; it only conducts recruitment examinations

options.label: D
options.text: The UPSC's advice is required only for Group A officers, not for Group B or C

questions.solution: Correct answer: The UPSC's advice is advisory, but non-consultation can invalidate the disciplinary order.

questions.text: The post of Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister:

options.label: A
options.text: Is a constitutional authority created under Article 77

options.label: B
options.text: Is created by executive order and derives authority from the Prime Minister's discretion

options.label: C
options.text: Has a fixed tenure of five years as per the Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules

options.label: D
options.text: Is appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet

questions.solution: Correct answer: Is created by executive order and derives authority from the Prime Minister's discretion.

questions.text: The Committee on Estimates differs from the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) in that:

options.label: A
options.text: The Committee on Estimates has 30 members from both Houses, while PAC has 22 members only from Lok Sabha

options.label: B
options.text: The Committee on Estimates examines proposed outlays for efficiency, while PAC audits past expenditure with the CAG

options.label: C
options.text: The Committee on Estimates can summon Ministers for evidence, while PAC can only call officials

options.label: D
options.text: The Committee on Estimates' reports are legally binding, while PAC's reports are only recommendatory

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Committee on Estimates examines proposed outlays for efficiency, while PAC audits past expenditure with the CAG.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the domestic legal effect of an executive agreement concluded by the President on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers?

options.label: A
options.text: It automatically becomes part of domestic law without any legislative action.

options.label: B
options.text: It is binding under international law but has no direct domestic effect unless implemented by a statute.

options.label: C
options.text: It requires ratification by Parliament under Article 253 before it can bind the Union.

options.label: D
options.text: It can amend the Constitution without a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It is binding under international law but has no direct domestic effect unless implemented by a statute..

questions.text: Regarding the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), which statement is accurate in light of recent procedural developments?

options.label: A
options.text: The Prime Minister can unilaterally appoint the CAG without any consultative mechanism.

options.label: B
options.text: The President appoints the CAG on the advice of the Council of Ministers, but recent rules mandate a selection committee.

options.label: C
options.text: The CAG is appointed by a collegium of judges similar to the higher judiciary.

options.label: D
options.text: The appointment of the CAG requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The President appoints the CAG on the advice of the Council of Ministers, but recent rules mandate a selection committee..

questions.text: The Cabinet Secretariat is best characterised as:

options.label: A
options.text: A political office akin to the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).

options.label: B
options.text: A permanent civil‑service body governed by the Transaction of Business Rules.

options.label: C
options.text: A constitutional authority established under Article 77 of the Constitution.

options.label: D
options.text: An ad‑hoc body constituted only during national emergencies.
