options.text: Intentional manipulation by the RBI to manage exchange rate expectations

options.label: D
options.text: Mismatches between customs data and foreign exchange transaction reporting only

questions.solution: Correct answer: Timing differences and coverage gaps in recording current and capital account transactions.

questions.text: India's exchange rate regime is best characterised as a 'managed float' because:

options.label: A
options.text: The RBI announces a fixed parity band and intervenes only when the rate breaches the band

options.label: B
options.text: The exchange rate is market-determined but the RBI intervenes to manage excessive volatility without targeting a specific level

options.label: C
options.text: The RBI pegs the rupee to a basket of currencies and adjusts the peg periodically

options.label: D
options.text: The exchange rate is fully market-determined with zero central bank intervention

questions.solution: Correct answer: The exchange rate is market-determined but the RBI intervenes to manage excessive volatility without targeting a specific level.

questions.text: Which macroprudential tool was used by the RBI during the COVID-19 pandemic to ease dollar funding pressures?

options.label: A
options.text: Imposition of a volatility cap on FPI holdings in government securities

options.label: B
options.text: Reduction of the short-term external commercial borrowing all-in-cost ceiling

options.label: C
options.text: A US$ 2 billion dollar-rupee swap window

options.label: D
options.text: Mandatory conversion of NRI deposits into rupee-denominated bonds

questions.solution: Correct answer: A US$ 2 billion dollar-rupee swap window.

questions.text: As of end‑March 2024, which of the following combinations correctly describes India's external debt position and a key sustainability indicator?

options.label: A
options.text: US$ 620 billion, 19.8% of GDP, debt‑service‑to‑exports ratio of 7.2%.

options.label: B
options.text: US$ 650 billion, 21.5% of GDP, debt‑service‑to‑exports ratio of 8.5%.

options.label: C
options.text: US$ 580 billion, 18.2% of GDP, short‑term‑debt‑to‑reserves ratio of 7.2%.

options.label: D
options.text: US$ 620 billion, 23.5% of GDP, debt‑service‑to‑exports ratio of 5.8%.

questions.solution: Correct answer: US$ 620 billion, 19.8% of GDP, debt‑service‑to‑exports ratio of 7.2%..

questions.text: What condition has the 2024‑25 Union Budget set for the gradual liberalisation of the FPI volatility cap by March 2026?

options.label: A
options.text: Establishment of a domestic central counterparty for government securities to enhance market depth.

options.label: B
options.text: Achievement of a current account surplus for four consecutive quarters.

options.label: C
options.text: Reduction of the external debt‑to‑GDP ratio below 15%.

options.label: D
options.text: Full convertibility of the rupee on the capital account.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Establishment of a domestic central counterparty for government securities to enhance market depth..

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the sunset‑review provision introduced by recent amendments to the Customs Tariff Act for trade‑remedy duties?

options.label: A
options.text: Anti‑dumping and countervailing duties continue automatically after five years without any review.

options.label: B
options.text: Duties terminate after five years unless a review demonstrates that expiry would lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury.

options.label: C
options.text: The sunset‑review clause applies only to safeguard measures, not to anti‑dumping or countervailing duties.

options.label: D
options.text: The review period is ten years, after which duties lapse if no review is conducted.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Duties terminate after five years unless a review demonstrates that expiry would lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury..

questions.text: Under the GATS framework, what do India’s Mode 4 commitments in bilateral agreements typically include?

options.label: A
options.text: Unconditional visa‑free entry for all skilled professionals.

options.label: B
options.text: Annual quotas for ICT professionals and fast‑track visa categories subject to labour‑market tests.

options.label: C
options.text: Permanent residency rights for service suppliers after two years.

options.label: D
options.text: Coverage under the WTO Services Waiver for Least‑Developed Countries.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Annual quotas for ICT professionals and fast‑track visa categories subject to labour‑market tests..

questions.text: What did recent legislative amendments do to the RBI’s external‑sector stress‑testing framework?

options.label: A
options.text: Made stress testing optional and removed the requirement to publish results.

options.label: B
options.text: Required the RBI to conduct stress tests only annually and report to Parliament.

options.label: C
options.text: Formalised the framework as a statutory obligation, requiring results to be presented to the Central Board within a defined period after each half‑year end.

options.label: D
options.text: Transferred stress‑testing responsibility from the RBI to the Ministry of Finance.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Formalised the framework as a statutory obligation, requiring results to be presented to the Central Board within a defined period after each half‑year end..

questions.text: Which feature was added to sovereign rating methodologies that explicitly incorporates the RBI’s swap‑line network?

options.label: A
options.text: A contingent‑liability metric for state‑owned enterprise guarantees.

options.label: B
options.text: A foreign‑currency liquidity sub‑factor.

options.label: C
options.text: A reserve‑adequacy ratio based solely on import cover.

options.label: D
options.text: A green‑bond issuance adjustment factor.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A foreign‑currency liquidity sub‑factor..

questions.text: According to the RBI's Reserve Management Guidelines (revised 2022) and the diversification strategy since 2018, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The guidelines set a maximum single-currency exposure of 80 per cent and a minimum gold share of 3 per cent

options.label: B
options.text: Gold's negative correlation with the dollar (approximately -0.4 over the past decade) improves the risk-adjusted return of the reserve portfolio, especially during dollar strength

options.label: C
options.text: SDRs are a static, non-yielding asset with an interest rate fixed at 0.5 per cent by the IMF Articles of Agreement

options.label: D
options.text: The liquidity-first hierarchy places tactical allocation to high-quality corporate bonds in non-reserve currencies at the top (priority 1) of the reserve structure

questions.solution: Correct answer: Gold's negative correlation with the dollar (approximately -0.4 over the past decade) improves the risk-adjusted return of the reserve portfolio, especially during dollar strength.

questions.text: According to the RBI's 2023 Survey on Invoicing Currency, what is the primary reason for the asymmetry between India's import-price and export-price exchange rate pass-through coefficients?

options.label: A
options.text: Higher dollar invoicing share for imports (86%) compared to exports (78%) leads to higher import pass-through

options.label: B
options.text: Exporters price in rupees while importers price in dollars, reversing the pass-through direction

options.label: C
options.text: Both coefficients are near unity due to complete pass-through in a fully open capital account

options.label: D
options.text: The RBI's intervention policy targets export prices more aggressively than import prices

questions.solution: Correct answer: Higher dollar invoicing share for imports (86%) compared to exports (78%) leads to higher import pass-through.

questions.text: What is the estimated relationship between daily turnover in the offshore rupee NDF market and the onshore forward market volume as reported by the RBI for 2023?

options.label: A
options.text: Offshore NDF turnover is roughly half the onshore forward market volume

options.label: B
options.text: Offshore NDF turnover is roughly equal to the onshore forward market volume

options.label: C
options.text: Offshore NDF turnover is roughly twice the onshore forward market volume

options.label: D
options.text: Offshore NDF turnover is negligible compared to the onshore forward market volume

questions.solution: Correct answer: Offshore NDF turnover is roughly twice the onshore forward market volume.

questions.text: Under the RBI's External Commercial Borrowings (ECB) framework, what is the mandatory hedging requirement for borrowers raising funds exceeding USD 20 million?

options.label: A
options.text: At least 50 per cent of ECB proceeds must be hedged for currency risk

options.label: B
options.text: At least 70 per cent of ECB proceeds must be hedged for currency risk

options.label: C
options.text: Hedging is optional but encouraged through a lower all-in-cost ceiling

options.label: D
options.text: Full 100 per cent hedging is required regardless of the borrowing amount

questions.solution: Correct answer: At least 70 per cent of ECB proceeds must be hedged for currency risk.

questions.text: Regarding the operational features of bilateral currency swap arrangements activated by the RBI, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Swap lines are unlimited in amount and tenor, providing a permanent source of foreign currency liquidity.

options.label: B
options.text: The interest rate on swap drawings is fixed at the policy repo rate of the providing central bank.

options.label: C
options.text: Each swap line has a maximum amount, a short tenor of typically three to six months, and an interest rate linked to the relevant OIS curve plus a spread.

options.label: D
options.text: Drawings under swap lines do not require sterilisation as they do not inject domestic currency liquidity.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Each swap line has a maximum amount, a short tenor of typically three to six months, and an interest rate linked to the relevant OIS curve plus a spread..

questions.text: Which of the following is a stated pillar of India's cross-border insolvency framework under the UNCITRAL Model Law adoption?

options.label: A
options.text: Automatic conversion of foreign debt into equity of the domestic corporate debtor.

options.label: B
options.text: Recognition of foreign proceedings with an automatic stay on domestic assets.

options.label: C
options.text: Exclusive jurisdiction of the NCLT over all global assets of the debtor, overriding foreign courts.

options.label: D
options.text: Mandatory liquidation of the corporate debtor upon recognition of foreign proceedings.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Recognition of foreign proceedings with an automatic stay on domestic assets..

questions.text: How does India's Green Finance Taxonomy integrate with the External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) framework to incentivise green projects?

options.label: A
options.text: By mandating that all ECBs above a certain threshold must be green-certified.

options.label: B
options.text: Through a 'green window' offering concessional all-in-cost ceilings and shorter minimum maturities for taxonomy-compliant projects.

options.label: C
options.text: By providing a sovereign guarantee for the principal repayment of green ECBs.

options.label: D
options.text: By allowing green ECBs to bypass the RBI's master direction on end-use restrictions entirely.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Through a 'green window' offering concessional all-in-cost ceilings and shorter minimum maturities for taxonomy-compliant projects..

questions.text: Regarding the Environmental Goods Agreement (EGA) negotiations at the WTO, what was India's core objection to the product list proposed by the coalition of 46 members?

options.label: A
options.text: The list included only goods relevant to climate mitigation and excluded adaptation technologies critical for the Global South, such as flood-resilient seeds and low-cost sanitation technology.

options.label: B
options.text: The list imposed non-tariff barriers on environmental services, violating the General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS).

options.label: C
options.text: The proposed tariff elimination schedule required immediate zero tariffs, without any special and differential treatment for developing countries.

options.label: D
options.text: The agreement sought to replace the UNFCCC's Technology Mechanism with a WTO-led technology transfer framework.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The list included only goods relevant to climate mitigation and excluded adaptation technologies critical for the Global South, such as flood-resilient seeds and low-cost sanitation technology..

questions.text: Under Article 112 of the Constitution, the Annual Financial Statement must distinguish between three specific funds. Which of the following correctly identifies these three funds and the key restriction on the Consolidated Fund?

options.label: A
options.text: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account; no money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund without parliamentary authorisation

options.label: B
options.text: Consolidated Fund, Emergency Fund, Public Account; withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund require only executive approval

options.label: C
options.text: Revenue Fund, Capital Fund, Contingency Fund; the Consolidated Fund can be accessed through ordinances

options.label: D
options.text: Consolidated Fund, Development Fund, Public Account; parliamentary authorisation is required only for capital expenditure

questions.solution: Correct answer: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account; no money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund without parliamentary authorisation.

questions.text: During the GST compensation shortfall in 2020-21, the Centre borrowed funds and passed them to States as back-to-back loans. What was the primary fiscal rationale for this mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: To preserve States' fiscal space without violating FRBM borrowing limits, while honouring the compensation guarantee

options.label: B
options.text: To increase the Centre's fiscal deficit temporarily while reducing States' debt-to-GDP ratios permanently

options.label: C
options.text: To shift the compensation burden to the RBI through monetised deficit financing

options.label: D
options.text: To allow States to exceed their FRBM borrowing limits with Centre's guarantee

questions.solution: Correct answer: To preserve States' fiscal space without violating FRBM borrowing limits, while honouring the compensation guarantee.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Medium‑Term Fiscal Policy Statement (MTFPS) and the Fiscal Strategy Statement (FSS) under the FRBM Act?

options.label: A
options.text: MTFPS sets annual policy actions while FSS provides a rolling three‑year fiscal framework.

options.label: B
options.text: MTFPS is a statutory rolling three‑year target document; FSS translates those targets into concrete annual policy actions such as expenditure prioritisation and borrowing plans.

options.label: C
options.text: Both MTFPS and FSS are identical documents presented together in the Budget.

options.label: D
options.text: FSS is a standalone document not linked to the Union Budget.

questions.solution: Correct answer: MTFPS is a statutory rolling three‑year target document; FSS translates those targets into concrete annual policy actions such as expenditure prioritisation and borrowing plans..

questions.text: The 15th Finance Commission recommended a guarantee commission rate of 0.5 % and a guarantee redemption fund for State guarantees. Which statement about the financing of this fund is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The guarantee redemption fund is financed by the commission, not the other way round.

options.label: B
options.text: The commission rate is 1 % and the fund finances the commission.

options.label: C
options.text: The fund finances the commission, making the commission dependent on the fund corpus.

options.label: D
options.text: The guarantee commission is optional and not linked to any redemption fund.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The guarantee redemption fund is financed by the commission, not the other way round..

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Treasury Single Account (TSA) as implemented by the Union Government?

options.label: A
options.text: Consolidated Fund

options.label: B
options.text: Contingency Fund

options.label: C
options.text: Public Account

options.label: D
options.text: State‑level provident fund accounts

questions.solution: Correct answer: State‑level provident fund accounts.

questions.text: Regarding the Expenditure Management Commission (EMC) recommendations, which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The EMC mandated universal zero‑based budgeting for all Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS).

options.label: B
options.text: The EMC recommended pilot zero‑based budgeting for CSS, not a blanket rollout.

options.label: C
options.text: The EMC recommended zero‑based budgeting only for Central Sector Schemes.

options.label: D
options.text: The EMC did not mention zero‑based budgeting at all.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The EMC recommended pilot zero‑based budgeting for CSS, not a blanket rollout..

questions.text: Which of the following operates as an automatic stabiliser in India without requiring fresh legislative action?

options.label: A
options.text: Discretionary stimulus packages announced under Atmanirbhar Bharat

options.label: B
options.text: Progressive personal income tax structure

options.label: C
options.text: Additional allocation for capital outlay in the Union Budget

options.label: D
options.text: Changes in the repo rate by the Monetary Policy Committee

questions.solution: Correct answer: Progressive personal income tax structure.

questions.text: With reference to Ways and Means Advances (WMA), which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: WMA is a primary tool for financing the fiscal deficit on a permanent basis

options.label: B
options.text: WMA is a cash-management facility that does not alter the fiscal deficit unless overdrawn

options.label: C
options.text: WMA is governed exclusively by the Government Securities Act, 2006

options.label: D
options.text: WMA interest rate is fixed at the repo rate for the entire financial year

questions.solution: Correct answer: WMA is a cash-management facility that does not alter the fiscal deficit unless overdrawn.

questions.text: In the context of Union Government finance, disinvestment proceeds are classified as:

options.label: A
options.text: Revenue receipts that reduce the revenue deficit

options.label: B
options.text: Non-debt capital receipts that do not affect the revenue deficit

options.label: C
options.text: Capital expenditure that increases the fiscal deficit

options.label: D
options.text: Tax revenue that improves tax buoyancy

questions.solution: Correct answer: Non-debt capital receipts that do not affect the revenue deficit.

questions.text: Which of the following accurately describes the function of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) in budgetary oversight?

options.label: A
options.text: It modifies budget allocations during the financial year based on expenditure trends

options.label: B
options.text: It reviews past expenditure and recommends corrective action but cannot modify budget allocations

options.label: C
options.text: It approves the annual government borrowing programme before it is placed in Parliament

options.label: D
options.text: It sets the fiscal deficit target for the medium term under the FRBM Act

questions.solution: Correct answer: It reviews past expenditure and recommends corrective action but cannot modify budget allocations.

questions.text: The Taxpayer Charter notified in August 2020 is legally enforceable through which of the following provisions?

options.label: A
options.text: Section 119A of the Income-Tax Act, 1961 and Section 171A of the CGST Act, 2017

options.label: B
options.text: Section 119 of the Income-Tax Act, 1961 and Section 171 of the CGST Act, 2017

options.label: C
options.text: Section 119A of the Income-Tax Act, 1961 only

options.label: D
options.text: Section 171A of the CGST Act, 2017 only

questions.solution: Correct answer: Section 119A of the Income-Tax Act, 1961 and Section 171A of the CGST Act, 2017.

questions.text: What is the IMF‑World Bank benchmark debt‑to‑GDP ceiling for emerging market economies under the Debt Sustainability Analysis framework?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 70%.

questions.text: According to the 2022‑23 Tax Expenditure Statement, what was the estimated total tax expenditure as a percentage of GDP?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 1.2%.

questions.text: Which feature characterises the 15th Finance Commission’s approach to state‑level fiscal rules?

options.label: A
options.text: Uniform FRBM targets for all states

options.label: B
options.text: State‑specific glide paths and performance‑based grants

options.label: C
options.text: Mandatory central approval for all state borrowing

options.label: D
options.text: Fixed debt‑to‑GDP ratio of 60% for every state

questions.solution: Correct answer: State‑specific glide paths and performance‑based grants.

questions.text: What does the Open Budget Survey (OBS) evaluate?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the Union Budget presentation

options.label: B
options.text: The entire budget cycle including legislative oversight and public participation

options.label: C
options.text: Only the CAG audit reports

options.label: D
options.text: Only the fiscal deficit numbers

questions.solution: Correct answer: The entire budget cycle including legislative oversight and public participation.

questions.text: In January 2023, the Government of India issued its first sovereign green bonds with which maturities?

options.label: A
options.text: 5‑year and 15‑year

options.label: B
options.text: 10‑year and 30‑year

options.label: C
options.text: 7‑year and 20‑year

options.label: D
options.text: 12‑year and 25‑year

questions.solution: Correct answer: 10‑year and 30‑year.

questions.text: Under the GST Council's decision‑making procedure, what is the voting weight distribution between the Centre and the States, and what majority is required for a decision?

options.label: A
options.text: Centre 1/2, States 1/2, simple majority

options.label: B
options.text: Centre 1/3, States 2/3, three‑fourths of weighted votes

options.label: C
options.text: Centre 2/3, States 1/3, two‑thirds majority

options.label: D
options.text: Centre 1/4, States 3/4, three‑fourths majority

questions.solution: Correct answer: Centre 1/3, States 2/3, three‑fourths of weighted votes.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the current application of Zero‑Based Budgeting (ZBB) in the Union Budget?

options.label: A
options.text: ZBB has been applied to the entire Union Budget since 2017

options.label: B
options.text: ZBB is limited to pilot centrally sponsored schemes reviewed by the Expenditure Review Committee

options.label: C
options.text: ZBB replaces the traditional incremental budgeting for all ministries

options.label: D
options.text: ZBB is mandatory for all capital expenditure proposals

questions.solution: Correct answer: ZBB is limited to pilot centrally sponsored schemes reviewed by the Expenditure Review Committee.

questions.text: How are pension liabilities treated in the Union Government's fiscal accounts with respect to the revenue deficit and FRBM compliance?

options.label: A
options.text: They are recorded as off‑budget items and excluded from revenue deficit

options.label: B
options.text: They form part of committed revenue expenditure and directly affect the revenue deficit and FRBM compliance

options.label: C
options.text: They are financed through a separate pension fund and do not impact the fiscal deficit

options.label: D
options.text: They are accounted as capital expenditure and thus not part of revenue deficit

questions.solution: Correct answer: They form part of committed revenue expenditure and directly affect the revenue deficit and FRBM compliance.

questions.text: Regarding spectrum auction proceeds, which statement correctly reflects their accounting in the Union Budget?

options.label: A
options.text: The full auction amount is recognised as non‑tax revenue in the year of auction

options.label: B
options.text: Only the annual instalment (after a moratorium) enters non‑tax receipts of a given fiscal year, as instalments are spread over 20 years

options.label: C
options.text: Spectrum proceeds are treated as capital receipts and added to disinvestment receipts

options.label: D
options.text: They are recorded as tax revenue under the GST compensation cess

questions.solution: Correct answer: Only the annual instalment (after a moratorium) enters non‑tax receipts of a given fiscal year, as instalments are spread over 20 years.

questions.text: The JAM trinity, which forms the architectural backbone of the Direct Benefit Transfer programme, consists of which three components?

options.label: A
options.text: Jan Dhan Yojana, Aadhaar, and Mobile

options.label: B
options.text: Jan Dhan Yojana, Aadhaar, and MGNREGA

options.label: C
options.text: Jan Dhan Yojana, Mobile, and UPI

options.label: D
options.text: Aadhaar, Mobile, and Unified Payments Interface

questions.solution: Correct answer: Jan Dhan Yojana, Aadhaar, and Mobile.

questions.text: With reference to Viability Gap Funding (VGF) in Public-Private Partnerships, which of the following statements is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: VGF is a pure grant that creates no contingent liability for the government.

options.label: B
options.text: VGF disbursements are accounted for in the headline fiscal deficit as capital expenditure.

options.label: C
options.text: Revenue-shortfall guarantees associated with VGF can trigger additional future outlays, creating contingent liabilities.

options.label: D
options.text: VGF is limited to 10% of project capital cost and is provided only as interest-free loans.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Revenue-shortfall guarantees associated with VGF can trigger additional future outlays, creating contingent liabilities..

questions.text: The District Mineral Foundation (DMF) funds are characterised by which of the following features?

options.label: A
options.text: They can be diverted to the State's general expenditure with legislative approval.

options.label: B
options.text: The contribution rate is 10% of royalty for major minerals and 30% for minor minerals.

options.label: C
options.text: They are managed by the Central Government and allocated to States based on population.

options.label: D
options.text: The contribution rate is uniform at 20% of royalty for both major and minor minerals.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The contribution rate is 10% of royalty for major minerals and 30% for minor minerals..

questions.text: In the context of India's fiscal-monetary coordination, Market Stabilisation Scheme (MSS) bonds are correctly described as:

options.label: A
options.text: A fiscal deficit financing instrument that appears in the fiscal deficit calculation.

options.label: B
options.text: A sterilisation tool used by the RBI to absorb liquidity from capital inflows, not counted in fiscal deficit.

options.label: C
options.text: Bonds issued by the Government to finance the current account deficit during outflow episodes.

options.label: D
options.text: Instruments that increase the Government's market borrowing programme and debt-to-GDP ratio.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A sterilisation tool used by the RBI to absorb liquidity from capital inflows, not counted in fiscal deficit..

questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding disaster risk financing in India: 1. Releases from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) automatically increase the corpus of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF). 2. The Contingency Fund of India has a corpus of ₹500 crore and is financed by the National Calamity Contingency Duty (NCCD). 3. The NDRF is financed through the NCCD and had a corpus of approximately ₹23,000 crore. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 3 only

options.label: D
options.text: 1, 2 and 3

questions.solution: Correct answer: 3 only.

questions.text: Which of the following sub-schemes is NOT bundled under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) as described in the National Food Processing Policy framework?

options.label: A
options.text: Mega Food Parks

options.label: B
options.text: Integrated Cold Chain

options.label: C
options.text: Food Safety and Quality Assurance

options.label: D
options.text: Price Stabilisation Fund

questions.solution: Correct answer: Price Stabilisation Fund.

questions.text: What is the fundamental design principle of the Mega Food Park (MFP) scheme that distinguishes it from traditional food parks?

options.label: A
options.text: MFP provides only fiscal incentives like tax holidays, leaving infrastructure development to the private sector.

options.label: B
options.text: MFP follows a hub-and-spoke model with a Central Processing Centre (CPC) linked to Primary Processing Centres (PPCs) and Collection Centres (CCs) for backward integration.

options.label: C
options.text: MFP mandates that all processing units must be owned and operated by Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs).

options.label: D
options.text: MFP is exclusively located in metropolitan areas to ensure proximity to export ports and high-end retail markets.

questions.solution: Correct answer: MFP follows a hub-and-spoke model with a Central Processing Centre (CPC) linked to Primary Processing Centres (PPCs) and Collection Centres (CCs) for backward integration..

questions.text: The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020 deregulated the stockholding limits for which category of commodities, subject to specific trigger conditions?

options.label: A
options.text: All foodgrains including wheat and rice under the National Food Security Act

options.label: B
options.text: Cereals, pulses, oilseeds, edible oils, onion and potato

options.label: C
options.text: Only perishable horticulture produce like fruits and vegetables

options.label: D
options.text: Only export-oriented processed food products

questions.solution: Correct answer: Cereals, pulses, oilseeds, edible oils, onion and potato.

questions.text: Which digital platform, operational since 2019, enables exporters to register farms, record input usage, and generate electronic certificates of origin and phytosanitary certificates for traceability?

options.label: A
options.text: NAM (National Agriculture Market)

options.label: B
options.text: APEDA's TraceNet

options.label: C
options.text: FSSAI's FoSCoRIS (Food Safety Compliance System)

options.label: D
options.text: ICEGATE (Indian Customs Electronic Gateway)

questions.solution: Correct answer: APEDA's TraceNet.

questions.text: The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) provides coverage for food processing MSMEs. What is the key reason for its low uptake in the sector despite offering up to 85 per cent loan coverage?

options.label: A
options.text: CGTMSE requires mandatory land titles and audited financials for all applicants

options.label: B
options.text: The scheme's uptake has stayed below 12 per cent because most processors are unaware of the simplified no-collateral window for loans up to ₹2 crore

options.label: C
options.text: CGTMSE coverage is restricted to primary processing units and excludes cold-chain infrastructure

options.label: D
options.text: The guarantee cover is only available for loans exceeding ₹5 crore

questions.solution: Correct answer: The scheme's uptake has stayed below 12 per cent because most processors are unaware of the simplified no-collateral window for loans up to ₹2 crore.

questions.text: Regarding the digital market integration platforms in agriculture, which statement correctly distinguishes the roles of e-NAM and ONDC?

options.label: A
options.text: NAM and ONDC are interchangeable platforms that both replace APMC legislation

options.label: B
options.text: NAM's primary mandate is price discovery for raw produce through a unified mandi platform, while ONDC is an open-commerce protocol operating at a different layer

options.label: C
options.text: ONDC has subsumed e-NAM and now handles all inter-mandi trade settlements

options.label: D
